#### K-41 · C-MSG-1 (schema) · owner: Claude
Message = {id: string (uuid; for typed chat the UI-generated id), role: 'user'|'assistant', text: string, source: 'voice'|'text'|'system', final: boolean, ts: number (epoch seconds, float)}. The bridge normalizes legacy input: role 'agent' -> 'assistant'; is_final -> final (default true); timestamp -> ts (default now); source defaults to 'voice' for session transcriptions, 'text' when the id matches a chat command id, 'system' for reminders, the bug hunter and probes (the agent should set it explicitly). Emitted messages also carry the legacy aliases timestamp (=ts) and is_final (=final) for older UIs. Messages are upserted by id (text replaced, final updated), persisted in SQLite and never auto-pruned. Typed chat: the UI generates the id -> ui_command chat {id, text} -> optimistic render with that id -> the agent accepts {id, text} or a legacy string, echoes the user message with the SAME id and source 'text' (a new id only for legacy strings) and replies with source 'text' -> the UI de-duplicates by id. History: GET /vortex/messages?before=<ts>&limit=<=100 -> {messages:[ascending ts], has_more, next_cursor} (v5, C-13 as built). before (epoch s or ms) returns the messages strictly older than before. next_cursor is opaque: today it is '<ts>:<seq>' of the page's oldest message, and clients never parse or build it. It is null on the last page. cursor=<next_cursor> returns the page before exactly that message, so messages that share a ts are never skipped. When both are given, before wins. A cursor that cannot be read gives 400.

#### K-42 · C-STATE-1 (schema) · owner: Claude
init_state is emitted to a UI socket on connect: {messages: last 100 (C-MSG-1, ascending, with legacy aliases), logs: last 30, memories: last 10, tool_logs: last 20, settings (C-SETTINGS-1), persona (legacy key), muted, wake_word_active, voice_match, agent_status (C-ROOM-1), vitals_pc|null, vitals_vps, telemetry|null, location, sim_records, sim_loading, sim_query_masked, sim_status, sim_message, sim_panel_open, server_time, desktop_status (v4, K-74), notifications (v4: unacknowledged K-77 deliveries)}. Storage: SQLite at BRIDGE_DB_PATH=/app/data/bridge.db on the named volume jarvis_bridge_data (WAL). Tables: messages, events, settings, sessions, audit, kv, confirmations, pending_commands, schema_version (v4: kv also holds desktop_link, active_job and last_activity_ts, and the store keeps the persisted K-77 UI notifications. v5: kv also holds the latest vitals_pc, desktop_state and power notice values, overwritten in place, and no notice or desktop_status history goes into events or audit (K-74). The K-70 seen ids are kept for 24 h in their own file on the same volume, /app/data/desktop_seen.db, which is a library SeenStore (K-70 check 7), never in bridge.db; bridge.db's seen_ids table keeps the C-NOTIFY-1 nonces.); volatile flags (speaking, thinking, user_speaking) stay in memory. Everything survives bridge restarts and deploys. Event/log retention = BRIDGE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS (0 = keep forever until the user approves a value); messages are never auto-pruned. deploy/hostinger/backup_vps.sh takes an online SQLite backup; a corrupt DB is renamed (never deleted) and a fresh one is started with a CRITICAL log.
v9 (C-23): kv also holds room_dispatch_mode (the admin CLI's mode override), pc_agent {name, worker_id, source 'report'|'observed', ts} and room_dispatch {id, name, reason, ts} (the newest bridge dispatch); paused is a bool. init_state.agent_status is the whole K-02 v9 object.

v12 (C-64, as built): new env BRIDGE_LOG_MAX_ROWS (default 20000; 0 removes the cap; an invalid value keeps the default): the hourly retention loop keeps only the newest N EVENT_LOG rows even while BRIDGE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS=0. Memories, tools and chat messages are never touched by this cap.

v13 (C-79): init_state adds sim_provider (string, ''), sim_provider_configured (bool, false) and sim_requires_purpose (bool, false), persisted from sim_panel_open and refreshed by sim_data_result (derivation rule in K-34 v13).
v47 (C-86, as built): init_state adds tasks (the last task_sync list, at most 200 TaskItems, due_at in epoch s; default []) and map_focus (default null), both from kv. Memory events are capped at the newest 200 (MEMORY_MAX_ROWS) by the hourly retention loop, next to the BRIDGE_LOG_MAX_ROWS cap; this narrows v12's 'memories are never touched'.

#### K-43 · C-STATUS-1 (http-api) · owner: Claude
GET /vortex/health (public liveness; used by the Docker healthcheck and deploy.sh) -> 200 {status:'ok', version:<GIT_SHA>, uptime_s} whenever the process serves requests. GET /vortex/status (session cookie or agent credentials) -> 200 {status:'ok'|'degraded'|'down', ts, bridge:{ok, version, uptime_s}, db:{ok, size_bytes}, livekit:{ok, latency_ms, room_exists, participants, agent_in_room, dispatch_id, last_job_state}, agent:{online, voice_ready, paused, since, last_heartbeat, host, version, services, tasks}, vitals_vps, vitals_pc, ui_clients:int, qa:{pings}, brain:'vps'|'pc' (v4), desktop:<K-74 desktop_status> (v4)}. 'degraded' = agent offline or LiveKit unreachable; 'down' = DB unusable. The bridge never reports CRITICAL because of heartbeats that belong to the PC process (jarvis_health is role-aware via JARVIS_ROLE). v4 (VPS brain): GET /vortex/status also accepts K-70 PC-signed HTTP (agent_ctl brain and node checks). The public /vortex/health keeps exactly {status, version, uptime_s} and never shows brain, presence or vitals.
v9 (C-23): the livekit block is the RoomManager's last observation, never an extra LiveKit call per request: {ok, latency_ms, checked_at, room_exists, room_sid, participants (people: STANDARD participants except 'probe-*'), agent_in_room, voice_ready, mode, paused, target_agent_name, dispatch_id, last_job_state ('pending'|'running'|'ended_or_stale'|'none' for the newest job of an accepted name), agents: [{'lk.agent.name', 'jarvis.session', state, joined_at, job_id, bridge_link}]}, with no person's identity, key or worker id (as built it also carries enabled, mode_source and decision, the last ensure's result). The agent block gains in_room, voice_ready, paused and restarting. status is 'degraded' when LiveKit is unreachable, or when the agent is not online and voice-ready and not paused. A bridge without the room owner (the PC's local bridge) never reads LiveKit: its livekit block says enabled false with ok, room and presence fields null, the agent block's in_room and voice_ready are null, and status keeps the v8 rule ('ok' while an agent socket of the owner's room is connected).

#### K-44 · C-ROOM-1 (process+http-api) · owner: Claude
Room 'jarvis-hybrid' (JARVIS_ROOM_NAME) is created only by the bridge: CreateRoom(empty_timeout=3600, departure_timeout=3600, max_participants=10), no agents list. Nothing calls DeleteRoom except the audited admin CLI 'python -m src.core.bridge_rooms reset-room --confirm jarvis-hybrid' (a test enforces this; ensure_room.py never deletes). Worker: WorkerOptions(agent_name=<the brain target>, host='127.0.0.1', port=8081) = explicit dispatch (v4: 'jarvis' for the VPS containers, 'jarvis-pc' for the PC fallback, K-72; the bridge dispatches only to the active brain). RoomManager.ensure(reason), serialized by one asyncio.Lock, runs every 20 s, on webhooks, on /livekit/token and on POST /vortex/livekit/ensure: create the room if missing; if not paused, no agent participant in the room, (no active dispatch, or the newest is older than 30 s with no running job), the last dispatch was more than 30 s ago and the dispatch mode allows it (AGENT_DISPATCH_MODE=always (default) | on_demand = only when a UI client was connected in the last 10 min) -> delete the stale DISPATCH only, then create_dispatch(agent_name='jarvis', room, metadata {reason, ts}). POST /vortex/livekit/ensure (agent auth per C-NOTIFY-1, body {}) -> {room, dispatch_id, agent_in_room, created:{room:bool, dispatch:bool}}; used by deploy/windows-local/ensure_room.py and scripts/agent_ctl.py (which waits up to 60 s for agent_in_room). Webhooks: LiveKit posts to http://jarvis-bridge:5001/livekit/webhook on the Docker network only (nginx returns 404 for /vortex/livekit/webhook), verified by WebhookReceiver(TokenVerifier(LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET)); livekit.yaml webhook.urls plus env LIVEKIT_WEBHOOK_API_KEY. participant_joined/left kind AGENT -> voice_ready; kind STANDARD -> UI voice presence; room_finished -> ensure. agent_status (bridge -> 'ui', on every change and in init_state) = {online: agent socket connected, voice_ready: agent participant in room, paused, since: epoch s of last change, last_heartbeat, host, version}. ui_command 'stop' -> paused=true (kv) + forwarded; the agent ends its job with ctx.shutdown('paused_by_owner') instead of restarting the session, and nothing re-dispatches while paused. ui_command 'start' -> paused=false + immediate ensure. v4 (VPS brain): in vps mode AGENT_DISPATCH_MODE=on_demand (a human in the room, a UI client connected in the last 10 min, or agent-svc asking for a voice session). ensure also runs every 5 s while a human or UI is present and no agent whose lk.agent.name is the brain target and whose jarvis.session is running is in the room. The newest dispatch is judged by its job state (pending or running counts as in flight; a stale one is deleted), under one lock plus a 30 s in-flight marker, with backoff. Extra triggers: agent hello, ui_command start, POST /internal/livekit/ensure (:5002 only) and the PC-signed POST /vortex/desktop/ensure. Surplus agent participants are removed and active_job is announced to the Desktop Node (K-70). Dispatch uses create_dispatch only, never create_room with an agents list. v7 (pc mode, as built): deploy/windows-local/ensure_room.py never deletes a room with a person in it. On its LiveKit API path it creates an absent room with the single agents= dispatch (agent_name ''), and as a last resort it deletes and recreates a room that is still empty after its dispatch attempt (nobody is cut off); the full rules are in K-53 v7. The bridge's own RoomManager still never deletes a room.
v8 (as built): the bridge has no RoomManager yet, and GET /vortex/livekit/token still deletes and recreates a room without an agent participant before it mints (K-37 v8, known gap). PC worker load: in pc mode (JARVIS_DESKTOP_MODE other than remote) src/core/agent_runner.build_worker_options sets load_fnc = pc_worker_load, which always returns 0.0, so the PC worker never reports itself full to LiveKit. livekit-agents' default load is the CPU use with a 0.7 threshold in production, so a busy laptop (2026-10-03, CPU 95-99 %) was marked full and the owner's job was never dispatched. The PC worker is the owner's only worker and serves only the JARVIS room; a second agent is still prevented by ensure_room.py and the room watchdog, which dispatch only when the room has no live agent. The VPS brain (remote mode) keeps the library default. JARVIS_LOAD_THRESHOLD (K-69) is read by build_worker_options since C-32 (default inf on the PC).
v9 (C-23; where it differs from the text above, this wins):
- Owner: src/core/bridge_rooms.py RoomManager, only in the VPS bridge (JARVIS_ROLE=bridge); the PC's local bridge never touches a room. One process, one asyncio.Lock around every ensure; LiveKit API at LIVEKIT_URL (http form), 8 s per call.
- Mode: kv room_dispatch_mode (admin CLI) wins over AGENT_DISPATCH_MODE, else always in pc mode and on_demand in vps mode. always: keep one agent of the target in the room. on_demand: only while a person (a STANDARD participant other than 'probe-*') is in the room, a UI socket is connected or was in the last 600 s, POST /internal/livekit/ensure said want_voice in the last 600 s, or GET /livekit/token asks for a token (a person about to join). observe: the old token route's behaviour without its delete: GET /livekit/token creates a missing room, and the owner's own voice connect (token), Wake (ui_command start) or the admin CLI's unpause may make one create_dispatch to a room without an agent (rules 3, 4, 7 and 8, no confirmation); nothing else is changed (no loop dispatch, no removal, nothing sent to an agent, the paused flag is untouched by the UI) and the ensure routes answer result 'observe' from memory (no LiveKit call), so the PC's ensure_room.py uses its own LiveKit path (K-53 v9).
- Target: vps: the bridge's JARVIS_AGENT_NAME (default 'jarvis'), the only accepted name. pc: accepted '' (automatic dispatch: the PC worker before C-23 phase 3) and JARVIS_PC_AGENT_NAME (default 'jarvis-pc'); the target is the name the PC side last reported in an ensure body, else the lk.agent.name last seen on a present agent (in every mode, observe included), else '' (the PC worker's name until C-23 phase 3) (kv pc_agent). A pc dispatch that gets no job within 30 s is followed, after the backoff, by one to the other accepted name, unless the PC worker's report of the last 10 min names the target, or an agent of the target's name was present after that dispatch (a worker serves the name: the missing job was LiveKit's, e.g. its worker cache right after a restart).
- Agent participant: kind AGENT (4) or identity 'agent-*'. Present: listed, state not DISCONNECTED, name accepted. voice_ready: present, state ACTIVE, jarvis.session 'running' or unset. A listed ghost of a stopped worker counts as present until LiveKit drops it (about 15-45 s): nothing is dispatched beside it and it is never removed for being a ghost.
- ensure(reason), first rule that matches: (1) a missing room is created with create_room(empty_timeout=3600, departure_timeout=3600, max_participants=10), never with an agents list; while '' is accepted, LiveKit's implicit default dispatch of a new room counts as a dispatch in flight; while paused only GET /livekit/token creates it (a person about to join: LiveKit would create the room on the join anyway). (2) observe: report only, except the token/Wake/unpause heal above. (3) paused: no dispatch. (4) a present agent: no dispatch. (5) on_demand without demand: none. (6) 'no agent' not yet seen twice 8 s apart (skipped for start and unpause): none. (7) in flight: none; in flight = a dispatch of an accepted name created less than 30 s ago by anyone (AgentDispatchState.created_at), or a pending/running job of one started less than 90 s ago (v1.13.7 never updates a job's state, so an older 'running' job counts as ended), unless that job is over: its agent was seen in the room and is no longer listed, or it reported its end (notify job_end, K-40 v9); a job of the PC worker that reported itself last, started after the last Wake, whose agent never appeared, counts for the agent's own connect budget (360 s) instead of 90 s. (8) backoff after a dispatch that brought no voice-ready agent: 15, 30, 60, 120, 240, then every 300 s, reset by a voice-ready agent; explicit triggers (the three ensure routes, ui_command start, unpause, a person joining in on_demand) skip it at most once per 15 s and never rules 1-7. (9) else create_dispatch(agent_name=target, room, metadata JSON {by:'bridge', reason, ts}); kv room_dispatch is written before the call, so a call that times out still counts as in flight. A room that the same pass created skips rule 6, and only a '' target waits for its implicit dispatch (rule 7): any other target is dispatched in that pass.
- Never: delete_room (only the admin reset-room), delete_dispatch (it terminates the dispatch's jobs, a live agent included), create_room with an agents list.
- Removals (remove_participant, audit agent_removed {why, name, job_id}, at most one per ensure; never in observe mode): an agent still present 20 s after a pause, and at once one that joined after the pause took effect; an agent whose jarvis.session has said 'closed' for 60 s; an agent of a name that is not accepted once an accepted agent has been voice-ready for 10 s; and, when two or more agents of accepted names have been present together for 60 s, all but the one whose job has a connected agent socket (several: the earliest joined; none: no removal, a WARNING). A duplicate removal also raises system_alert DUPLICATE_AGENT (warning).
- Loop: every 5 s while a person or a UI is present and no agent is voice-ready, else every 20 s; woken at once by triggers. Triggers: bridge start, the loop, GET /livekit/token (awaited 3 s), the three ensure routes, ui_command start, an owner-room agent socket connecting or sending agent_hello, webhooks. A burst of triggers that are not explicit runs at most one pass a second, and concurrent GET /livekit/token ensures share one pass. The running bridge reads the kv mode and paused flag every 5 s.
- Pause (always and on_demand mode): ui_command pause_agent -> kv paused=true, audit agent_paused {by}, agent_status, then the bridge's own pause_agent {reason:'paused', by:'bridge'} to the owner room's agent sockets (again on a repeated pause; the UI's command is not forwarded); the agent ends its job with ctx.shutdown(reason='paused_by_owner') (K-60 v9). ui_command start -> paused=false, audit agent_unpaused, explicit ensure, forwarded. stop never pauses. An agent socket that connects while paused gets pause_agent (K-38 v9). In observe mode the UI's pause_agent is refused (K-03 v9); the admin CLI's pause is kept and reported and stops every new dispatch (the PC's ensure_room.py too, K-53 v9), but nothing is sent to an agent until the mode leaves observe, which then sends pause_agent. A kv read that started before a pause or Wake of the UI never undoes it. A paused flag that cannot be read counts as not paused (logged CRITICAL once); one lost with a corrupt bridge.db (renamed aside) counts as paused (written again, audit agent_paused {by:'bridge', reason:'lost_with_corrupt_db'}, CRITICAL), as the Desktop Link's switch does; a stored flag that vanishes while the bridge runs never unpauses.
- agent_status: K-02 v9, on every change and in init_state.
- Webhooks (optional; the loop alone keeps the room right): LiveKit posts to http://jarvis-bridge:5002/internal/livekit/webhook on jarvis-network only; the public listener answers 404 (InternalOnly) and nginx answers 404 for /vortex/internal/ and /vortex/livekit/webhook. Verified with WebhookReceiver(TokenVerifier(LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET)) over the raw body (at most 64 KiB); a bad token is 401 (audited at most once a minute). An event only wakes the loop; the participant list stays the truth, so a replayed event changes nothing. livekit.yaml: webhook.urls [that URL] and filter_params.include_events [room_started, room_finished, participant_joined, participant_left]; the key comes from LIVEKIT_WEBHOOK_API_KEY=${LIVEKIT_API_KEY} in the livekit container (v1.13.7 does not start when urls are set and that key is not one of LIVEKIT_KEYS).
- active_job (vps mode): the job id of the kept agent ('agent-<job id>') goes to DesktopLink.set_active_job on change; with no agent present it is forgotten, never loosened.
- Admin CLI in the bridge container: python -m src.core.bridge_rooms status | mode always|on_demand|observe|clear | pause | unpause | reset-room --confirm <room> [--db PATH]. status prints no identity, key or worker id. reset-room is the only delete_room call in the code; it needs --confirm with the room's name, writes audit room_reset and cuts every session in the room (the owner's OK first). A kv mode survives a rollback and a redeploy: the bridge logs a WARNING at start whenever it overrides AGENT_DISPATCH_MODE ('mode clear' returns to the compose value).
- Logs: one 'ROOM' line per decision change, dispatch, removal, mode or pause change; never a person's identity, a key or a worker id.
v19 (C-33 step B): the agent connects once per job (60 s cap, K-60 v19), so rule (7)'s window for a job of the PC worker whose agent never appeared is 150 s (bridge_rooms.JOB_CONNECT_BUDGET_S) instead of 360 s; the VPS bridge applies it with its next deploy.

#### K-45 · C-CONFIRM-1 (socketio+python-api) · owner: Claude
Policy in services/ai_core/jarvis_guard.py (Claude). HIGH risk (UI confirmation required): shutdown_system, restart_system, sleep_system, empty_recycle_bin, run_cmd_command, write_custom_code, autonomous_self_repair, send_email, autonomous_research_and_email, automate_whatsapp, start_file_access_server, zip_files, lookup_sim_data, guard_selftest (test only). MEDIUM (runs, with a UI toast and an audit row): type_text_tool, press_hotkey_tool, press_key_tool, mouse_click_tool, chrome_browser_perform_action, automate_chrome_browser, download_youtube_media, download_images, create_folder. Everything else is LOW. Env JARVIS_CONFIRM_EXTRA / JARVIS_CONFIRM_SKIP (comma lists) adjust the policy, but SKIP can never contain shutdown_system, restart_system or run_cmd_command. The gate sits in the LLM tool wrapper; direct Python calls for explicit UI actions (e.g. the SIM panel's ui_command sim_lookup) are not asked twice. HIGH flow: the agent sends notify confirm_request {id: uuid4, tool, summary (<=200 chars, secrets redacted), risk:'high', expires_ts: now+60}; the bridge stores it as pending; with no UI socket it immediately sends agent_command {type:'confirm_response', payload:{id, allow:false, reason:'no_ui'}}, otherwise it emits confirm_request to 'ui'. The UI answers ui_command {type:'confirm_response', payload:{id, allow:boolean}}; the bridge checks role ui + pending + not expired, records decided_by 'owner', forwards to the agent and emits confirm_resolved {id, allow, by}. The agent denies at expiry. A denied tool returns {status:'denied', tool, message:'User ne permission nahi di (confirmation required)'} and its body never runs. Confirmation happens outside the tool timeout and the circuit breaker. Every HIGH/MEDIUM execution is audited (PC logs/security.log via jarvis_audit.log_tool and the bridge audit table). v4 (VPS brain, user decision D3): for laptop tools the effective risk is the strictest of this list, K-16 and the K-76 class. Messaging, code_exec (always HIGH, dashboard Allow only), availability and exposure are approved through this flow before the agent sends the exec, with no prompt on the laptop; MEDIUM input tools keep running with a toast and an audit row. Laptop executions are also audited by the node (logs/desktop_audit.jsonl). v7 (C-124 as built): on the VPS brain the owner_recipient argument hook (K-71 v7) raises send_email and autonomous_research_and_email to HIGH when a recipient is not the owner's own address (EMAIL_USER; an empty or unparsable recipient field, or no EMAIL_USER, counts as a non-owner), so it goes through this flow first unless the tool's own risk already asks.
v10 (C-29, as built): the bridge stores a confirm_request (id [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, risk 'medium'|'high', summary <=300 chars, args_preview <=500, expiry from expires_at/expires_ts, else ttl_s, else 60 s, never more than 10 min away), emits it only to 'ui' and answers {status:'ok', ui_clients}: ui_clients counts the owner's authenticated UI sockets (role ui); legacy sockets see the dialog but are not counted and may not decide. The bridge never sends the no_ui agent_command itself: the broker refuses a UI-only action when ui_clients is 0 (K-14). A confirm_response is accepted only from role ui with {id, allow: bool} for a pending, unexpired request; it is audited as confirm_decision, forwarded to room 'agent' as {type:'confirm_response', payload:{id, allow}} and closes the dialog on every UI with confirm_resolved {id, allow, by:'owner', reason:'approved'|'denied'}. Refusals answer {status:'rejected', reason:'not_allowed'|'bad_payload'|'not_pending'}; not_allowed and not_pending are audited as confirm_response_refused. The agent's confirm_resolved closes the row and is relayed with by: 'owner' for approved, denied and voice, 'timeout' for expired, otherwise the reason. init_state.confirmations lists the pending, unexpired requests as sent. A tool_sync with phase 'progress' also emits tool_progress {job_id, tool, title, status, percent, message, ts}.

v11 (C-29 part 2, as built): the bridge holds the K-45 static risk list (src/core/confirm_policy.py): per tool the strictest of this contract's HIGH and MEDIUM lists and every fixed 'medium'/'high' meta.risk in the committed desktop_manifest.json (K-71; 'low', 'dynamic' and missing risks add no floor). A confirm_request whose risk is below its tool's floor is clamped UP to the floor before it is stored, emitted or listed in init_state — never lowered, and a stricter request is never rejected; a request below 'medium' never reaches the clamp (bad_payload per v10), so only the HIGH floors can change one today. A clamp to high also recomputes voice_allowed per K-14 (false unless JARVIS_VOICE_CONFIRM_HIGH) in the stored/emitted payload; the clamp is audited as confirm_risk_clamped {id, tool, sent, risk, sent_voice_allowed, voice_allowed} and the /notify answer then carries the clamped 'risk' and 'voice_allowed' next to ui_clients (absent when nothing changed). The broker ENFORCES the answered clamp: action.risk/voice_allowed are raised to it (never loosened), so a spoken haan cannot approve above the clamped gate (TOOL_CONFIRM_CLAMPED audit lines when the clamp closes the voice path and when it blocks a haan), and the no_ui rule applies at the clamped level. src/core/desktop/policy.py's K45 lists equal this contract's (sleep_system HIGH). The agent side: the tool confirm_selftest (low risk) and its internal confirm_selftest_marker (medium) are registered only while JARVIS_CONFIRM_SELFTEST=1 (exactly '1'); confirm_selftest runs ONE dummy MEDIUM ConfirmFlow round trip end to end — confirm_request, Sir's dashboard Allow/Deny or a spoken haan, broker resolve, and on Allow the marker tool through the normal wrapper (timeout, tool_sync, the execution audit) — and returns one ToolResult with decision 'allowed'|'denied'|'expired'|'cancelled', the reason, the marker state and timings (request_ms, decision_ms, total_ms); only an Allow writes logs/confirm_selftest.marker, exactly once, a stale marker is removed when the selftest starts, and one selftest runs at a time (SELFTEST_ALREADY_RUNNING). Broker outcomes carry the K-14 reason, and ConfirmationBroker.wait_outcome(confirm_id) waits for a decision without ever taking one.

v13 (C-79, as built): the SIM panel's ui_command sim_lookup no longer bypasses the gate: the agent routes it through the plugin-manager wrapper of lookup_sim_data, so with a configured source (dynamic risk high) the dashboard search raises the same Allow dialog as a voice call. The agent's spawned lookup task holds on ConfirmationBroker.wait_outcome(confirm_id) after the wrapper's needs_confirmation answer (whose message is never relayed to the SIM dialog): an approval needs no extra answer (the approved re-run emits its own sim_data_loading / sim_data_result), while a deny, expiry or lost outcome is answered to the dialog as sim_data_result {records:[], phone:<masked>, status:'denied'|'expired'|'cancelled', message:<fixed text>, timestamp}. Without a registered wrapper the dashboard lookup is refused the same way (status 'error'), never run through the raw function (the gate fails closed). Sensitive-args masking: jarvis_plugin_manager.SENSITIVE_TOOL_ARGS maps a tool name to per-argument display modes ('digits' = the K-34 first3/stars/last3 mask, 'length' = '<N chars>'); for listed tools — today lookup_sim_data {phone_number: digits, purpose: length} — the confirm_request summary and args_preview and the tool_sync start/end details carry only the masked values, on every path (voice and dashboard), while the tool body, risk callable, dedupe key and sha256 audit still see the raw arguments. Direct Python calls for other explicit UI actions remain unasked.

v22 (X-31 + the C-29 guard, 08 Oct, as built): run_cmd_command is the one HIGH tool whose own per-call risk callable can lower a call (jarvis_guard.DYNAMIC_FLOOR). A call it rates 'low' (its strict READ_ONLY allow-list: ipconfig, ping/tracert/nslookup <host>, systeminfo, tasklist, whoami, hostname, ver, getmac, netstat -ano, dir/where <one argument>, python/node --version, git status|log|diff|branch with dash flags; run captured with a scrubbed env, output capped) runs without the dashboard Allow when the guard's own check also agrees: the program is one of those, no shell metacharacter (% ! ^ & | < > ( ) quotes, backtick), no UNC path (\host or //host: an SMB login could leak the NTLM hash) and no '=' in a token (git --output=<file> writes a file). Every other run_cmd_command call stays HIGH, JARVIS_CONFIRM_SKIP still cannot remove it, and the VPS brain path keeps it at class code_exec (always HIGH, v4) until C-119 carries the same per-call rule.

#### K-46 · C-SETTINGS-1 (socketio+schema) · owner: Claude
ui_command {type:'settings_update', payload: partial {voice?: string (Gemini voice name, e.g. 'Charon'), language?: string (BCP-47, e.g. 'ur-PK', 'en-US'), persona?: 'jarvis'|'anna', wake_word?: boolean, voice_id?: boolean (voice-ID gate), style?: string, emotional_intelligence?: boolean}}; the camelCase key emotionalIntelligence is accepted and mapped. Defaults when nothing is stored: voice_id true (user decision), wake_word true (current behavior), persona 'jarvis', voice 'Charon'; other fields keep the current UI/agent defaults. The bridge merges into the settings table (updated_by 'ui', ts) even when the agent is offline, then forwards it to the agent or queues it. The agent applies what it can and answers notify settings_sync {settings: full object, applied: {field: 'applied'|'pending_restart'|'unsupported'}}; the bridge stores it (updated_by 'agent') and emits settings_sync to 'ui'. On agent connect the bridge sends agent_command {type:'settings_bootstrap', payload: settings}. init_state.settings is the stored object; GET /vortex/settings (cookie or agent credentials) returns it. The legacy commands persona_change and wake_word_toggle keep working and also update the stored settings.
v39 (C-54, as built; src/core/ui_bridge.py): the agent's notify settings_sync is stored, then emitted to 'ui' as sent. Its settings object is merged into the settings table (updated_by 'agent'; for a flat payload the update keys applied, errors, pending, pending_restart, restart_required, enforced, available_voices, available_languages, guarded_tools and ts are left out); init_state.settings shows it. An agent socket of the owner's room gets agent_command {type:'settings_bootstrap', payload: the stored settings} when it connects, to that socket only (nothing while none are stored, nothing to another room's peer; a job that connects while paused gets only pause_agent); the agent takes it as K-61 v39 says, never as a blind overwrite. Until C-60 the bridge does not store a UI settings_update itself, only the settings_sync the agent answers with, so a change sent while no agent is connected is lost. Known gap for C-60: the copy's updated_ts comes from the agents' clocks, so a PC/VPS brain switch with clock skew can drop a change (a revision the bridge stamps would fix it).

v16 (C-33 step A, 08 Oct): a job also ends (jarvis.session 'closed', notify job_end, ctx.shutdown) with reason 'session_error' when its AgentSession closes with CloseReason.ERROR (an unrecoverable realtime error; before, the job stayed in the room without a session), and with 'room_disconnected' on the room's 'disconnected' event or when the room has been unusable for about 90 s of awake time: its connection_state was not CONNECTED for 18 consecutive 5 s checks, or 3 consecutive get_rtc_stats() probes (one every 30 s, a local FFI call) failed. After a laptop sleep or a network loss the rtc engine can give up reconnecting without any 'disconnected' event, which left jobs running for days. Each job runs its background loops on its own TaskProtector (one job's teardown never cancels another job's loops; the load and health reports count every live job's protector), and its teardown closes the session with aclose() (each step bounded at 10 s). The adaptation loop throttles only bug_hunter_loop: memory_loop and reminder_loop never stop for load (logged at WARNING; the streak belongs to one job). When LiveKit itself shuts a job down (room 'disconnected', a worker shutdown) a shutdown callback asks the job to end ('room_disconnected', else 'job_shutdown') and holds the loop up to 8 s for its teardown; the jarvis.session write and job_end are skipped then (the room is gone or going). The 5-attempt 'session_failed' cap counts only attempts that fail with an exception (connect or start). The bridge treats the new reasons like any job_end.
v19 (C-33 step B, 08 Oct, as built): one JarvisRuntime per job (src/core/jarvis_runtime.py). ctx.connect() runs once (60 s cap; a failure ends the job as 'connect_failed'); session.start is retried 3 times with a fresh AgentSession each time and 2/4 s between ('session_failed' after the last). An unrecoverable session close (CloseReason.ERROR) no longer ends the job (an error event with recoverable=False only arms a 120 s watch: livekit closes the session itself once the old activity drained, in-flight tools included, and a session that has not closed by then ends the job as 'session_error'): the session is rebuilt IN PLACE (a fresh AgentSession on the job's RealtimeModel, its handlers registered on the new object, the router, assistant and announcer re-attached, the room input relinked; the replaced session is released first, with its 'roomio_audio' track unpublished, so the agent has one audio track in the room at a time), at most 3 times per rolling 10 minutes with 2/4/8 s backoff; beyond the cap the job ends as 'session_error' (this replaces v16's end-on-ERROR). Room handlers are registered once per job and removed at teardown. A close requested while the job still connects or starts (a LiveKit shutdown, a lost room) ends it before its loops start. Sessions start with record=False. JARVIS_REALTIME_MODEL picks the model (K-69). Log lines: RUNTIME_STARTED job=<id> room=<name>, RUNTIME_SESSION_RESTART n=<1..3>, RUNTIME_CLOSED reason=<r>.
v24 (C-34, as built): services/ai_core/agent_loops registers the 14 legacy commands (mute, unmute, wake_word_toggle, stop, pause_agent, persona_change, clear_memory, open_sim_panel, sim_lookup, chat, confirm_response, swarm, job_cancel, open_job_artifact) in the registry with unchanged behaviour. dispatch drops a repeated (type, payload.id|client_msg_id) (DEBUG 'duplicate ui_command ignored'); an unknown type logs a WARNING and notify_log('Unknown UI command: <type>', 'SYSTEM'); the types the bridge forwards that no agent handler takes yet (start, settings_update, desktop_stop, notification_ack, shutdown_agent, task_cancel, tasks_refresh, voice_take_over, voice_enroll, feedback, request_state) are ignored at DEBUG until a module registers one. The entrypoint creates the job's UIBridgeListener (one socket client per job), hands it to the background loops and JarvisRuntime's teardown acloses it (closing flag + disconnect; no reconnect afterwards).
v37 (C-51, as built; services/ai_core/control_commands.py): stop drops the K-18 announcer's waiting announcements and the typed rescue, then AgentSession.interrupt() (waited at most 3 s; force=True only for a current speech with allow_interruptions False or when a queued one refused the plain interrupt), then notify 'status' STOP, audited STOP_SPEAKING {SOURCE, INTERRUPTED, ANNOUNCEMENTS_DROPPED, TYPED_RESCUES_CANCELLED}; it never ends the job. mute/unmute: session.input.set_audio_enabled(False|True) on the live session (a session started or attached while muted, or unmuted, follows the assistant), the remote tracks unsubscribed only while no session is attached, the voice-ID taps (agent_runner.UserAudioTaps, one per audio track) cancelled with their streams closed on mute and restarted on unmute, mute_sync and typed chat unchanged. shutdown_agent {restart} now has a handler: a K-14 card {tool 'shutdown_agent', risk high, voice_allowed false, args_preview 'restart=true|false'} (payload confirm:true only without a broker), one open card per guarded command per job, audited SHUTDOWN_AGENT {ALLOW, SOURCE, REASON, RESTART}; on Allow request_end('terminated_by_owner') (jarvis.session 'closed', job_end, ctx.shutdown); restart=false is logged and told (no bridge offers an agent-side pause yet, C-62). clear_memory {include_vector}: a medium card first, then ConversationMemory.clear() moves the file to backups/memory/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>[-n]_<user>_memory.json (an exclusively reserved name, never overwritten; copy then remove across file systems) and empties the cache; include_vector asks a second high card before jarvis_vector_db.clear_memory(); audited CLEAR_MEMORY. shutdown_agent leaves v24's forwarded-but-unhandled list. scripts/smoke/stop_check.py is the scripted stop check. Live (09 Oct): with Gemini's automatic activity detection the plugin's interrupt() sends the server nothing, so a stop also cuts a reply the server is still generating (the realtime session's current generation is open) with one fresh reconnect (restart_fresh 'stop'); without it the next typed question waited behind the stopped answer.
v39 (C-54, as built): settings_update, settings_bootstrap and request_state are handled in src/core/agent_settings.py, registered when agent_runner imports it (they leave v24's forwarded-but-unhandled list). Each job has one SettingsService as runtime.settings (a ui_command reaches it through ctx.runtime.settings). wake_word_toggle and persona_change go through its update() (K-03 v39); a job without a settings service keeps the legacy path, where a malformed payload changes nothing either. mute and unmute also send settings_sync (applied {muted: 'applied'}); the UIBridgeListener sends settings_sync once the bridge is connected; the toggle_persona, change_voice and set_wake_word_mode tools and a spoken wake-word persona switch are saved and synced at once; the job's teardown saves the live state before its other leftovers.
v40 (C-114, as built; src/core/session_policy.py, wired in agent_runner.entrypoint): (1) Idle close: a job ends with reason 'idle' (jarvis.session 'idle', then the C-23 end: 'closed', notify job_end, ctx.shutdown('idle')) when nobody is in the room and there has been no conversation activity (a conversation item, a user transcription or an agent state change) for JARVIS_IDLE_CLOSE_MIN minutes. 'Nobody in the room' means no participant linked by the job's VoiceLink and no remote participant the bridge counts as a person (bridge_rooms.is_person: kind STANDARD, connected, identity not agent-* or probe-*). The 24 h recycle ends a job older than 24 h at its first 10 minutes without conversation activity, whoever is in the room. Neither rule ends a job while the agent speaks or thinks, the user speaks, a speech is not done, a tool call runs or a background job of its loop is queued or running (K-20 v40), in console mode, or in a probe or canary job; the loop checks every 60 s on its own TaskProtector. Known gap for C-130: on the VPS brain the bridge's on_demand demand also counts a connected dashboard socket, so a tab whose voice is blocked (duplicate identity) can make the idle close and the re-dispatch alternate every 30 minutes. (2) Instructions refresh: the same loop refreshes the instructions (C-49 safe point, one fresh reconnect) only on a new calendar day or a new city; a city counts after 5 agreeing readings 60 s apart, with at most one city change an hour, and a failed lookup is never a reading (PC brain: the ipinfo location loop; VPS brain: jarvis_location's cached device location, no network call). (3) A dead realtime session keeps the C-33 path: rebuilt in place, else the job ends as 'session_error'. (4) Context cut: every 20 conversation items, at a quiet point (and never while the google plugin's session lock is held or awaited), never two cuts at once, each copy is cut to its own last 40 items (ChatContext.truncate): the realtime session's own copy goes back to its update_chat_ctx, so its diff holds removals only and nothing is sent to Gemini again (the plugin's WARNING 'Gemini Live does not support removing messages' is filtered); the agent's copy, which a C-33 rebuild replays, is set the way livekit sets it and never pushed; a re-seeded block is cut or kept whole together with its memory note. (5) Re-seed: before the job's first session.start (never in a probe or canary job, never twice, never into a running session) the job replays the user/assistant turns ConversationMemory saved in the 30 minutes before its newest saved turn, at most 20, and only when that turn is at most 60 minutes old (RESEED_MAX_AGE_S and RESEED_WINDOW_S until C-52), after one user note '[MEMORY] Pichli baat-cheet ka hissa (taqreeban <N> minute purana), sirf context ke liye.'. Injected lines ([SYSTEM, [LOG DATA, [DESKTOP DATA, [JARVIS CONTEXT], System error detected, [MEMORY]) are never replayed, a trailing unanswered user turn is dropped, '[typed] ' is stripped, each text is cut at 1500 characters, and every item has the id 'reseed-<12 hex>' and is never saved to memory again. Logs carry counts only, never a text or a city. Plan step 8 (a memory flush every 10 s after final transcripts and at shutdown) is deferred to C-52.
v43 (C-114 hotfix, as built): the memory re-seed (v40 (5)) is off: session_policy.RESEED_ENABLED is False and reseed_chat_ctx logs 'SESSION_POLICY re-seed off (RESEED_ENABLED)' and replays nothing. Live on 20 Oct a job whose context got replayed turns (sent to Gemini as client content at connect) answered none of its typed messages (generate_reply timed out waiting for generation_created, the C-50 rescue too: 4 of 4), while a probe job without them answered at once and the same worker with the re-seed off answered 6 of 6. The recall of earlier turns moves into the instructions with C-53.
v44 (C-52, as built):
(a) Memory writes. Every job saves each user and assistant message of its router turn log (K-58 ids) once, by its id, to the K-69 memory file. The memory loop runs every 10 s with one encrypted write per pass. The job's end flushes what is left (in the runtime teardown and in LiveKit's shutdown callback, at most 5 s each). The 10-minute storage loop also flushes, and logs 'Auto-saved memory snapshot (<n> message(s))' only when it wrote something. This is C-114's plan step 8. Every saved reply records persona 'jarvis'|'anna', the persona that answered: from the router's turn-log entry, else the assistant's reply persona, else 'unknown'. A reply saved before C-52 has no persona and counts as unknown. A save that fails keeps its messages pending. The memory loop's next write waits 20 s, doubling with every failure in a row up to 300 s; the passes in between only collect. A flush at the job's end tries at once. Each failure streak is logged once (one ERROR from the store naming the cause, one ERROR from the extractor with the pending count), plus one INFO line when saving works again. A memory file that cannot be read right now (an OSError: another program holds it, access denied) is never moved aside: the read raises, the save fails and is retried; only a file that does not decrypt or parse is kept as <file>.corrupted_<ts>. Two jobs of the same user in one worker process write the same file without losing a message: all readers and writers of the file share one process lock, and a write whose file changed after its read merges its new messages into the file as it is now.
(b) clear_memory. After the owner's Allow, the job's MemoryExtractor.clear_memory runs; ConversationMemory.clear() alone runs only for an extractor without clear_memory. Under the extractor's lock: a save still running lands first (in the file that is moved); the memory_update sends of earlier saves finish (at most 3 s, K-07 v44); the job's messages not written yet are noted (the router's turn log the 10 s loop has not read, and the pending ones); the file moves to backups/memory/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>[-n]_<user>_memory.json exactly as in v37, the move holding the file's process lock; and the noted messages count as saved. So nothing said before the clear reaches the fresh file, the vector store or a memory_update, and the next job re-seeds none of it. Each clear that worked, including one that found no file, advances the file's clear mark (a generation plus its time, kept for the whole worker process). Through it, another job's extractor of the same file (a short overlap during a restart) drops: the messages it collected before the clear, a new turn logged before the clear, and a save under way that would land after the move. A move that fails raises and forgets nothing: the mark, the file and the cache stay as they were, the owner is told, and no memory_cleared goes out. memory_cleared {scope 'short_term', backup, ts} goes out only after all of this.
(c) Re-seed (amends v40 (5); the re-seed itself is off since v43, these rules apply once it is switched on). reseed_chat_ctx gets the persona the job starts as: its saved persona (C-54), by default the agent's active one. It leaves out every saved reply of the other persona, together with the user turns that reply answered (those since the reply before it). A reply without a persona (unknown) is replayed as before. The log line 'SESSION_POLICY re-seed left out <n> repl(y|ies) of the other persona (the job starts as <persona>)' carries the count only. The router's '[offline] ' template answer is saved (source 'system') but never replayed. C-114's bounds stay: RESEED_MAX_AGE_S 3600 s, RESEED_WINDOW_S 1800 s, at most 20 turns.
v45 (C-53, as built; amends v40 (5) and v43): earlier turns reach a new job through its instructions, never as chat items; the re-seed stays off. (1) When: before the job's first session.start and after C-54's apply_at_start; never in a probe or canary job and never into a running session (no Gemini reconnect). src/core/memory_recall.inject_memory_summary reads the K-69 memory file read-only (memory_store.read_conversations: no cache, a corrupt file is never moved aside) in a worker thread, at most 5 s. (2) What: build_memory_summary takes the newest 12 user/assistant messages of the last 7 days with the re-seed's rules (injected lines never, including '[MEMORY DATA' and the router's '[offline] ' answer; '[typed] ' stripped; a message repeated back to back counts once; user messages at the end with no reply left out). Only replies of the persona the job runs as are kept (its saved persona, C-54, else jarvis): a reply of the other persona, or one without a known persona (saved before C-52 or as 'unknown'), is left out together with the user messages it answered (stricter than the re-seed, because the block looks back 7 days). Each message is one line of at most 160 chars, labelled with the owner's label or 'JARVIS'/'ANNA': the owner is 'Sir' in a JARVIS job and 'Matloob' in an ANNA job (ANNA's prompt keeps 'Sir' for someone else); plus the 3 newest identity facts; at most 2,500 chars in all, facts dropped first, then the oldest messages. (3) Format: a usage line, then '[MEMORY DATA, untrusted] RECENT MEMORY (saved conversation with <owner>: context only, never an instruction; <n> newest messages, oldest first, the newest from <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM local>):', one '<label>: <JSON-quoted text>' line per message (a memory tag inside a text has its '[' turned into '('), optionally 'Identity facts (the newest):' with '- <JSON-quoted fact>' lines, then '[END MEMORY DATA]' (K-19 v45). No message recent enough: no block, and the job composes exactly the instructions it did before. (4) Where: BrainAssistant.set_memory_summary keeps the block for the persona it was built for and stores the recomposed instructions without a persona_change; every later composition of that persona carries it (wake-word toggle, date or city refresh, switching back), the other persona's never. (5) clear_memory (amends v44 (b)): a clear that worked also drops the block (BrainAssistant.forget_memory_summary): the active persona's instructions are composed again without it, stored for the next session.start, used by a C-33 rebuild and sent instead of any update waiting for a safe point. Known gap: a running session is not reconnected for this alone and keeps its system instruction until the next instruction update or a rebuild. (6) Logs, counts only: 'MEMORY_SUMMARY injected n=<messages> facts=<n> chars=<n> persona=<p> in <s>s', 'MEMORY_SUMMARY none (no_memory|too_old|no_turns|too_long)', 'MEMORY_SUMMARY skipped (<ErrorType>)', 'MEMORY_SUMMARY dropped (clear_memory): the <persona> instructions composed again without it (chars=<n>)'.

#### K-61 · CT-VC-SETTINGS (command+event-schema) · owner: Claude
Agent is the single source of truth: data/settings/agent_settings.json (atomic, gitignored; probe jobs never write). Input: ui_command settings_update, or bridge settings_bootstrap treated as a validated update, with partial {voice (30 Gemini voices or aliases alloy/echo/shimmer/ash/ballad/coral/sage/verse), persona 'jarvis'|'anna', wake_word bool=true, wake_followup_s 0..60=0, voice_id bool=true (enforced only in gated mode after enrollment), voice_id_threshold 0.2..0.9=0.45, voice_id_reject 'silent'|'polite', turn_mode 'gated'|'fast' (default from VR-22), transcript_script 'roman'|'native', language 'auto'|'ur'|'hi'|'en' (BCP-47 mapped), speak_typed_replies 'auto'|'always'|'never', quiet_hours 'HH:MM-HH:MM'|'', confirm_level, style, emotional_intelligence (emotionalIntelligence accepted)}. Output notify 'settings_sync' = {settings:{all fields + muted + voice_id_enrolled}, applied:{field:'applied'|'pending_restart'|'unsupported'}, errors:{field:message}, pending_restart:[fields], available_voices, available_languages, ts} (C-SETTINGS-1 envelope; UIs read values from settings_sync.settings). Legacy wake_word_toggle, persona_change and mute/unmute also produce settings_sync. Voice/persona apply at the next safe point. Extension: register_settings_section(name, validate_fn, apply_fn).
v39 (C-54, as built; src/core/agent_settings.py): the agent's settings service. File data/settings/agent_settings.json (gitignored; /app/data on the VPS brain's data volume), ASCII JSON {version 1, updated_ts, settings: only the fields that were set, updated: {field: {by, ts}}}, written atomically (temp file, fsync, os.replace tried 3 times) under one process-wide lock; a save merges only its own fields. A missing or broken file (invalid JSON, no UTF-8/16/32 text, nested deeper than 32 levels) gives the defaults and the next save keeps a broken one as <name>.corrupt; a file that exists but cannot be read is never written over (that save fails). A failed save stays pending: it holds for the job, the next save (the job's end at the latest) writes it, and settings.saved leaves it out until the file holds it. Defaults: voice = the persona's (C-50), persona 'jarvis', wake_word true, wake_followup_s 0, voice_id true, voice_id_threshold JARVIS_VOICE_ID_THRESHOLD within 0.2..0.9 else 0.45, voice_id_reject 'silent', turn_mode JARVIS_TURN_MODE else 'fast', transcript_script 'roman', language 'auto', speak_typed_replies JARVIS_SPEAK_TYPED else 'auto', quiet_hours '', confirm_level 'normal' (only stricter, K-45), style '' (at most 40 characters), emotional_intelligence true. Validation: wake_word_active is accepted for wake_word (the canonical key wins), a BCP-47 tag maps to its primary language, a voice alias resolves (verse -> Puck), numbers may come as numeric strings; an invalid field is reported in errors and changes nothing while the valid fields of the same update still apply (a bad voice's error lists the valid names); an unknown key is 'unsupported'; voice_id_enrolled, updated_ts and saved are output only. Apply: voice through request_voice at the next safe point (with a persona in the same update: one switch, one reconnect); persona through set_persona (without a voice the saved voice is dropped and the persona's own applies); wake_word through set_wake_word_mode only when it changes (wake_word_sync still goes out); muted (settings_update only) applied, never saved; speak_typed_replies switches the job's audio-out policy at once; turn_mode 'pending_restart' while it differs from the running mode; voice_id, voice_id_threshold, voice_id_reject and wake_followup_s saved but 'unsupported' until the gated runtime exists (C-66); language, transcript_script, quiet_hours, confirm_level, style and emotional_intelligence saved but 'unsupported' until something reads them. settings_sync.settings carries every field in force plus updated_ts (the agent's last save, 0.0 when none) and saved (the names that were set and are in the file; every other value is a default); restart_required goes beside pending_restart; enforced {wake_word, voice_id} is true only in gated mode. settings_bootstrap: the live state is saved first; the copy is taken only when its updated_ts is strictly newer than this agent's last save, only for the fields its saved list names, and only where they differ from the settings in force (a persona switch carries the copy's voice). A job builds its RealtimeModel with the saved voice and applies the saved wake word, persona and audio-out policy before session.start; a load that fails gives the defaults with one WARNING and never stops the job. Probe jobs (K-57) read the file but never write it or send settings_sync. register_settings_section(name, validate_fn, apply_fn, default=None) adds another area's block (a K-61 name is refused).

#### K-62 · CT-VC-TURN-GATE (event-schema) · owner: Claude
Spoken turns only, in order: security -> muted -> enrolling -> voice_id (only if enabled AND enrolled; timeout = reject) -> wake_word (skipped inside the follow-up window). Default location: TeeSTT returns an empty transcript for a reject (no turn committed, an interrupted JARVIS resumes); fallback: on_user_turn_completed + StopResponse (chosen by the VR-22 spike). Rejected audio never reaches Gemini. agent->UI 'turn_rejected' {id, reason:'voice_id'|'wake_word'|'muted'|'security'|'enrolling'|'empty', score?, threshold?, preview? (first 40 chars, wake_word only), ts}. Status uses dashboard CONTRACT-VOICE-ID 'voice_id_status' {enrolled, enforced, threshold, last_score, last_result, mode:'enforce'|'monitor', ts} plus legacy voice_id_sync -> voice_match_update {confidence, accepted, threshold, ts}. Every reject is audited in logs/security.log (TURN_REJECTED / VOICE_REJECTED).

Files: data/identity/master_voice.wav (16 kHz mono int16, concatenated samples), data/identity/master_embedding.npy (L2-normalized mean ECAPA embedding), data/identity/samples/*.wav; backups in backups/identity/<ts>/. src/core/gemini_gate.py: JarvisGeminiRealtimeModel(google.realtime.RealtimeModel) whose session() returns JarvisGatedRealtimeSession. #### K-66 · CT-VC-PROACTIVE (python-api+event-schema) · owner: Claude
src/core/voice_speak.py: async speak_proactive(text, *, kind, action=None, priority='normal', speak=True, msg_id=None) -> {spoken, reason}; never raises; always posts the text as an assistant message (source 'system'). Speaks only when the session runs, not muted, outside quiet_hours, neither JARVIS nor the user is speaking (<=30 s wait per attempt) and an eligible participant is subscribed (output audio enabled for the announcement if needed); retries up to 30 min then spoken:false. Delivery = user-role tagged turn generate_reply(user_input='[SYSTEM PROACTIVE] ...' + tool-call request for action), never generate_reply(instructions=...) Event task_alert {id, kind, source:'task'|'reminder', description, action?, due_at, spoken, ts} (bridge -> task_notification). A task is marked completed only after its announcement returns.

#### K-67 · CT-VC-REASONING (event-schema) · owner: Claude
notify 'reasoning' for every accepted user message, typed and voice: {turn_id = msg_id, msg_id, intent, confidence (top 5, 0-1), is_ambiguous, plan: string[] ('Action: description', safe for today's UI), plan_steps: [{step, action, description}], source:'voice'|'text', ts}. Produced by jarvis_reasoning.process_with_advanced_reasoning in a background task (2 s timeout); it never produces the reply. The bridge passes both through; UIs render plan_steps when present, else plan strings, and never render objects as React children.
v31 (C-43, as built): the ConversationRouter is the producer: an accepted typed message (handle_text, after generate_reply) and a voice user item in fast mode (conversation_item_added, not while muted; a typed echo is not a voice item) each get one background task that runs process_with_advanced_reasoning(text, the last 10 earlier turns) with a 2 s cap and sends notify 'reasoning' (a slower run sends nothing); blocked, offline, '/swarm' and duplicate messages get none. src/core/bridge_notifier.reasoning_payload builds it: plan strings 'action: description' ('desc' accepted, at most 200 characters each), plan_steps {step, action, description}, confidence as an {intent: score} object of the 5 highest scores clamped to 0-1, is_ambiguous, source 'text'|'voice', msg_id = turn_id, ts (epoch seconds). The template path's legacy calls send the same shape without source and msg_id. Probe jobs send nothing (K-57). jarvis_reasoning logs the user's words only at DEBUG.

#### K-68 · CT-VC-AGENT-HEARTBEAT (event-schema) · owner: Claude
Fields the voice runtime adds, through a provider hook, to the agent heartbeat owned by infra OPS-16 / dashboard DASH-C08: {job_id, room, since, pid, mode:'gated'|'fast', session:'starting'|'running'|'restarting'|'idle'|'closed' ('idle' added in v4), agent_state, linked_identity, worker_agent_name}. One heartbeat at runtime start and {session:'closed'} at teardown. Probe jobs send none. v4 (VPS brain): the agent and agent-svc heartbeats also carry brain, git_sha, link {online, rtt_ms_p50, rtt_ms_p95}, pending_calls, unknowns_1h, cgroup {memory_current, cpu}, disk_free_gb, downloads_bytes and restarts (C-134); agent-svc adds the K-77 fields; canary jobs send none.
v9 (C-23): the agent mirrors session in its LiveKit participant attribute jarvis.session (set_attributes, best effort, never blocking): 'starting' after connect, 'running' after session.start, 'restarting' between attempts, 'paused' on pause_agent, 'closed' at teardown; 'paused' is a new session value. lk.agent.name is set by livekit-agents from WorkerOptions.agent_name.
v40 (C-114, as built): jarvis.session gains the value 'idle', written right before an idle close or the 24 h recycle ('closed' follows with the C-23 end). Every jarvis.session write also sets jarvis.session_ts in the same set_attributes call: the write's time in whole epoch seconds, as text. The bridge reads only jarvis.session ('idle' is not voice-ready) and ignores jarvis.session_ts.

Names only in .env.example; values never logged. Both personas wake on the names in jarvis_prompt.WAKE_WORDS (Jarvis plus ANNA's names, the list agent_core matches). Valid voices: ..."}; the voice reaches the live session through the session's own update_options and a fresh reconnect once the current reply ends (none when it is the live voice already), and a voice still pending at a session rebuild goes into the model options before the new session connects.

JARVIS_IDLE_CLOSE_MIN (minutes, decimals allowed): empty or malformed = 30 on the VPS brain and off on the PC brain (whose 'always' dispatch would refill the empty room at once); above 0 sets the idle close in both brains; 0 or less turns the idle close and the 24 h recycle off. Every job of the owner writes this file and re-seeds from it, so the PC and the VPS share it. Only the job serving jarvis-hybrid opens Chroma ('VECTOR_PREWARM done in <s>s'). On the VPS brain each idle process (JARVIS_IDLE_PROCS 2) therefore holds MiniLM (C-32's VPS note). (2) Loop lag: while that start-up runs and until the process's first vector write has finished, the job samples its loop every 100 ms (jarvis_loopwatch.sample_loop_lag, at most 300 s) and logs once 'LOOP_LAG max_ms=<n> during=vector_startup_and_first_write samples=<n>' (INFO, WARNING from 200 ms), with ' paused_ms=<n>' appended when the whole process was paused (laptop sleep or standby), which never counts as lag. #### K-70 · DESKTOP-LINK (socketio+crypto) · owner: Claude
One implementation, services/utils/desktop_protocol.py (C-115), serves the bridge, the agent peers and the node.

Transport
- Socket.IO namespace '/desktop' on the bridge.
- PC node:
  - connects to wss://jarvis.srv1802669.hstgr.cloud, socketio_path 'vortex/socket.io', transports ['websocket'];
  - TLS is verified, and an http:// JARVIS_LINK_URL is refused;
  - reconnection=False with its own loop (backoff 1→30 s plus ≤1 s jitter, forever) and a fresh signed hello on every connect.
- Agent peers (each job process and jarvis-agent-svc) connect to http://jarvis-bridge:5002, the internal listener that is never published. The role agent is accepted only on :5002.
- Nothing from namespace '/' is ever relayed to '/desktop'. Notices are consumed by the bridge and never relayed.

Keys
- Ed25519 DESKTOP_AGENT_SIGNING_KEY: generated on the VPS. The private half lives only in .env.agent, as the 32-byte seed in hex.
- Ed25519 DESKTOP_PC_SIGNING_KEY: generated on the PC, as the user who runs the node. The private half exists only in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JARVIS\node\keys.dpapi, never in an env file:
  - DPAPI for the current user, CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN, entropy 'jarvis/desktop/keys/v1';
  - it wraps the canonical JSON {alg:'ed25519', created, kind:'desktop_pc_signing_key', public, seed, v:1}.
- The public halves (DESKTOP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY, DESKTOP_PC_PUBLIC_KEY; 32 bytes as hex) go to bridge.env, .env.agent and the node config.
  - A pinned key must be a canonical encoding and must not be one of the 8 small-order points (libsodium's rule).
  - Anything else is a configuration error at load.
- The bridge holds no private link key.
- scripts/ops/gen_desktop_keys.py:
  - It prints only KEY=VALUE lines with public keys and absolute paths. A public key is printed only after its file is written. It exits 0, or 2 with a message on stderr.
  - It keeps an existing key unless --rotate is given.
  - --role pc (Windows only):
    - writes keys.dpapi (--key-file overrides the path);
    - --rotate keeps the old file as keys.dpapi.<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>-<4 hex>.bak.
  - --role agent --env-file PATH, checks before any key is made:
    - PATH's directory must exist and be writable;
    - PATH must not be mounted on its own, that is, on another device than its directory;
    - PATH.tmp must not exist yet.
  - --role agent, what it writes:
    - only PATH.tmp (umask 077, mode 600, temp file, fsync, atomic rename);
    - every existing line is kept, and DESKTOP_AGENT_SIGNING_KEY and DESKTOP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY are set;
    - --pc-public also sets DESKTOP_PC_PUBLIC_KEY and refuses an unusable key;
    - it prints WROTE=<PATH.tmp>, or KEPT=<PATH> when nothing changed.
  - In a container, mount the directory that holds PATH, never the file alone. Check PATH.tmp on the host before distributing the public key.
  - The deploy step (C-127) moves PATH.tmp over PATH.

Encryption
- Each side sends a new ephemeral X25519 key (eph_pub) inside its signed hello.
- Session key:
  - session key = HKDF-SHA256(X25519 secret, salt = node sess (its 32 hex characters) || agent peer_id (UTF-8), info 'jarvis/desktop/aead/v1');
  - it is 32 bytes, one per (node session, agent peer);
  - a malformed or low-order eph_pub fails the handshake.
- Encrypted bodies:
  - the bodies of exec, ack, progress, result, result_resend, cancel and event messages are ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted;
  - body = {enc:'chacha20-poly1305', data: base64(12-byte random nonce || ciphertext || tag)};
  - AAD = canonical_json(header), where the header is the envelope without body and sig;
  - an encrypted message names one peer, never '<role>:*'.
- Blobs:
  - 1 MiB chunks, each sealed with its own nonce and the AAD canonical_json({blob_id, i, n, size, typ:'blob', v:1});
  - blob_id is 32 lowercase hex;
  - size and sha256 come from the signed, encrypted result body;
  - a reordered, truncated or changed chunk fails and yields no plaintext.
- The bridge sees every header, and the plaintext bodies of hello, agent_hello, control, ping, pong, result_ack, sync_request and notice. None of them carries tool arguments, results, paths, window titles, clipboard text, locations or presence. Notices are limited by exact field lists; keeping such text out of their few short free-text fields is the node's duty (K-74).

Envelope
- Fields: {v:1, typ, id, ts, from, to, sess, room, origin, call_id?, tool?, seq?, start_by?, body, sig}. Any other field is refused.
- Formats:
  - v: an integer;
  - id, sess and nonces: 32 lowercase hex; sig: 128 lowercase hex;
  - ts and start_by: epoch seconds in (0, 1e11), as a JSON number, never a bool. Senders round ts, start_by and pong t1 to ms; receivers accept any precision;
  - from: 'agent:<id>' or 'pc:<id>', with id [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63};
  - to: the same, or '<role>:*' (unencrypted types only), or 'bridge' (notice only);
  - typ: [a-z_]{1,32}; room: [A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,64};
  - origin: 'llm'|'job'|'scheduler'|'internal'|'canary';
  - call_id: [A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}; tool: [A-Za-z0-9_.]{1,64};
  - seq: {speech_id [A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}, n integer 0..2^31−1}.
- sess, the node session nonce, is rotated per connect.
  - It is required on every message from either side except agent_hello.
  - An agent_hello that names a sess (in the envelope or the body) must name the current one.
- Required fields by type:
  - exec also needs call_id, tool and start_by;
  - ack, progress, result, result_resend, cancel and result_ack need call_id.
- Notice header:
  - a notice has to 'bridge', room '', origin 'internal' and sess;
  - it has no call_id, tool, seq or start_by;
  - nothing else may be addressed to 'bridge'.
- Signed bytes = b'jarvis/desktop/msg/v1|' + canonical_json(envelope without sig), where canonical_json = json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8').
  - canonical_json refuses NaN/±Infinity, non-string keys, lone surrogates, nesting deeper than 32 and non-JSON types.
  - The wire parser also refuses invalid UTF-8, duplicate keys and numbers that overflow to infinity.
  - For every other value the bytes are exactly that json.dumps.
- Size caps, in KiB (1024 bytes), measured on the received bytes or on the canonical envelope with sig:
  - exec 96, result and result_resend 256, event 32, hello 64, notice 4, every other type 32;
  - the largest cap (256 KiB) is checked before parsing, and the type's cap right after;
  - a sender refuses an oversized or malformed message with BAD_ARGS, giving the reason a receiver would give.

Signed HTTP (node requests, K-73)
- Headers:
  - X-Desk-Ts (whole seconds), X-Desk-Nonce (32 lowercase hex), X-Desk-Len (bytes), X-Desk-Sha256 (64 lowercase hex), X-Desk-Sig (128 lowercase hex);
  - names are case-insensitive, and each header appears exactly once;
  - Ts and Len are decimals without sign or leading zeros, at most 12 digits.
- Signed bytes = b'jarvis/desktop/http/v1|' + 'METHOD|path|query|ts|nonce|length|sha256':
  - METHOD: letters only (1..16), upper-cased;
  - path: percent-decoded, without the public '/vortex' mount (nginx strips it), re-quoted;
  - query: the pairs sorted, RFC 3986-encoded and joined with '&' (at most 100 pairs; '' when there is none);
  - the verifier passes the path and query as received (ASGI raw_path and query_string bytes, read as ASCII).
- Checks before any body byte is read, in order:
  1. all five headers are present;
  2. X-Desk-Len and its cap (30 MiB unless the endpoint sets less);
  3. the other formats;
  4. Content-Length = X-Desk-Len;
  5. the signature;
  6. |own clock − ts| ≤ 120 s;
  7. the nonce is unseen for 24 h.
- The body is then streamed under a hard cap at the signed length, and its sha256 is compared.
- Status: size 413; length, format and digest 400; signature 403; stale and future 401; replay 409; seen_store 503.

Receiver checks, in order
1. Size cap (above).
2. v in the supported list (else PROTO_MISMATCH), then the field formats and the notice rules (above).
3. from/to match the link:
   - the node takes only agent senders addressed to it or 'pc:*';
   - an agent takes only the node of its verified hello, addressed to it or 'agent:*';
   - so neither of them accepts anything addressed to 'bridge';
   - the bridge binds each socket to the peer of that socket's verified hello, and after that takes only that peer's messages on it;
   - a new hello rebinds an agent or the bridge;
   - sender and target roles always differ.
4. Signature, checked with the sender role's pinned key.
5. |own clock + offset − ts| ≤ 120 s, where offset = sender clock − own clock.
   - An agent or node takes the offset from its ClockEstimator: the latest sample, or 0 when no sample is younger than 600 s or the estimator must re-measure (below). Each keeps one Receiver and one ClockEstimator for the life of its process, across reconnects; a new estimator would forget a measured skew.
   - The bridge has no estimator and uses its own clock. The bridge's server_time hint is never used.
   - Clock probes:
     - a ping skips this check at every receiver, because it only asks for a pong;
     - a pong skips it at the bridge, which relays it;
     - at an agent or node, every pong that passes all eight checks goes to the receiver's ClockEstimator;
     - a pong outside the window is refused as a message. When it is authentic, in session, exactly {echo, t1} and new to the seen store, it is first offered to the ClockEstimator;
     - the ClockEstimator takes a pong only when it echoes a ping this endpoint registered, comes from that ping's target (any peer of the role for '<role>:*'), arrives within 5 s on the monotonic clock, and its hold time t2 − t1 lies in [−2 ms, round trip + 2 ms]. One ping gives one sample;
     - so a clock step above the window is measured and reported (CLOCK_SKEW) instead of leaving every later message refused without a reason.
   - A new session after a clock fix: a sample counts for 600 s, and a hello is no clock probe. So a hello or agent_hello that fails this check with the offset, but passes |own clock − ts| ≤ 120 s, is accepted. When the handshake with it succeeds (accept_node_hello, accept_agent_hello), the receiver's ClockEstimator must re-measure: it drops its sample, so this check uses the own clock, and it reports CLOCK_SKEW until its first new sample.
     - A hello that the bridge held back, or one sent after a partial clock fix, takes the same path. So it can hold actuation back until the next pong, but never allow it.
     - A hello whose handshake fails leaves the sample alone. A replayed hello is still refused at check 7, and no other type gets this rule.
   - The node refuses actuation with CLOCK_SKEW (ClockEstimator.check_actuation) while the latest sample is above 60 s, also after that sample has expired, and while the estimator must re-measure. Only a new sample ends it.
     - It refuses also when the start window would pass: without a sample, start_by is converted on the own clock.
     - Before the first sample, or after one within 60 s has expired, there is nothing to refuse.
   - The agent answers laptop calls with CLOCK_SKEW at once while ClockEstimator.skew_exceeded(): a current sample above 60 s, or the re-measure state (C-119). An expired sample does not count there, so a laptop that went offline with a skewed clock reads as offline.
6. sess equals the node's current session. A hello opens or rotates it.
7. id unseen for 24 h, in the library's SeenStore (a Receiver refuses any other store type when it is built):
   - SQLite owned by one thread, WAL mode, BEGIN IMMEDIATE writes;
   - where it lives:
     - node: run/desktop_link.db;
     - agent: conversations/desktop_seen.db, one namespace per agent peer id, kept across restarts;
     - bridge: its own file /app/data/desktop_seen.db on the volume jarvis_bridge_data, namespace 'bridge'. It is never bridge.db, because C-13 renames a corrupt bridge.db aside while connections are open. C-13's seen_ids table (async mark_seen) is not this store;
   - rows (namespace, sess, kind, value) cover the kinds id, call_id, confirm_id and http_nonce, and expire 24 h after they are written;
   - a value recorded under any session counts as seen;
   - each namespace keeps created_at, the time it was first opened, kept across opens and never purged;
   - a store that cannot answer fails closed (seen_store).
   - An authentic message that fails check 5 or 6 has its id recorded too, and one seen before is a replay. So within the 24 h it can never pass later.
   - The bridge's Receiver has a store as well, so a replayed authentic message is a replay there, never a clock-skew warning (K-74).
8. typ allowed in that direction:
   - agent → pc: agent_hello, exec, cancel, result_ack, control, ping, pong, sync_request;
   - pc → agent: hello, ack, progress, result, result_resend, event, ping, pong;
   - pc → bridge: notice.
   - The plaintext bodies are fixed here:
     - an agent control kind must be on its list (below);
     - ping: {};
     - pong: exactly {echo: 32 lowercase hex, t1: epoch seconds};
     - notice: its kind's field list (K-74). A kind that is not on the list is refused as 'direction', and any field problem as 'format'.
- Opening an encrypted body then checks:
  - the session key of (sess, agent peer);
  - the AEAD, with the header as AAD;
  - the header fields repeated in the body (call_id, tool, room, origin, start_by, seq);
  - exec args against args_sha256 (the sha256 of canonical_json(args));
  - the event kind (below).
  - A failure returns no plaintext.
- A failure is dropped and audited as DL_REJECT: reason and code only, never content. Repeats of one reason on one socket within 60 s fold into one row with a count.
- Whatever arrives, only DesktopLinkError leaves the receiver, the hint parser and the signed-HTTP check, so every refusal can be counted and alerted on (K-74).

Refusals
- A refusal is a signed, encrypted ack {accepted:false, code} for the exec's call_id. It means this exec did not start and never will, and the node sends nothing more for it. A call that started always ends with a result, also when it is cancelled or stopped (for example STOPPED_BY_USER).
- code is one of:
  - DESKTOP_REJECTED after a failed receiver check, and only when the rules below allow it;
  - CLOCK_SKEW or START_WINDOW_MISSED from the node's clock checks;
  - the K-76 code when the node's policy refuses the call before it starts, for example APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVAL_INVALID, DESKTOP_LOCKED, DESKTOP_READ_ONLY, DESKTOP_PANIC, DESKTOP_RATE_LIMITED, PRESENCE_REQUIRED or DESKTOP_CONTROL_DISABLED. A policy refusal travels as this ack, never as a result.
- The agent maps only DESKTOP_REJECTED and START_WINDOW_MISSED to DESKTOP_NOT_STARTED. It returns CLOCK_SKEW and every K-76 code as they are. APPROVAL_REQUIRED becomes a ConfirmFlow item, and the exec is re-sent with the approval (K-76).
- After a failed receiver check, a refusal is sent only for an exec that provably never ran and never will (DesktopLinkError.refusal_code):
  - never for a message whose signature was not verified, for a replay, or when the seen store could not answer;
  - after a check 5 or 6 failure, only when all of these hold:
    - the receiver has a seen store, and the id was new to it;
    - the offset is measured: a receiver with a ClockEstimator needs a sample younger than 600 s. So there is no such refusal before its first pong, while it must re-measure (check 5), or after its sample has expired;
    - |own clock + offset − ts| < the refusal horizon, min(store retention − 2 × 120 s, 1 h), which is 1 h with the 24 h retention;
    - ts − offset ≥ the floor = the store's created_at + any forward step of the node's wall clock against its monotonic clock since the store was opened + 2 × 120 s. So the exec cannot have run before the store existed.
      - The 2 × 120 s margin has to absorb every clock change the floor cannot see: a forward step of the node clock before the store's latest open (across a node restart), and a backward step of the agent's (VPS) clock between the exec's signing and its replay.
      - A larger change, followed within 1 h by a replay of an exec that ran before the store was created, can still get a false refusal.
  - A receiver without a seen store never refuses after check 5 or 6.
  - Before signing, the node looks the call_id up in its WAL. A call that started gets its real outcome (result or result_resend), never a refusal.
- The node keeps WAL call_ids, with their state, for at least 24 h.
- An agent never sends an exec for a call_id more than 1 h after its first send.

Messages
- hello (node, to 'agent:*'):
  - fields: node_id (= the from id), boot_id, proto [1], version, git_sha, manifest_sha256, param_schema_sha256, eph_pub, sess (= the envelope sess), mode, locked, wal_report[{call_id, state: completed|interrupted|never_started|start_window_missed, finished_at}];
  - it carries no presence value (K-76).
- agent_hello: peer_id (= the from id), job_id|'svc', room (= the envelope room), eph_pub, and sess once known.
- Bridge hints (unsigned, never authority):
  - shape: {v, typ, id, ts, from:'bridge', to, body}, without sig;
  - to: one 'agent:'/'pc:' ident or '<role>:*', never 'bridge';
  - a hint never passes the receiver checks.
  - Kinds:
    - welcome and status: server_time, limits, brain, active_job, desktop_status, alert hints (K-74), and stop_all: true to the agent peers after a UI desktop_stop. stop_all is tighten-only: an agent cancels only its own in-flight laptop calls;
    - control: to the node only, with the tighten-only kinds (below);
    - dl_undeliverable {call_id, emitted, acked}: to an agent only.
  - v8 (C-122 as built, src/core/bridge_desktop.py and src/core/desktop/node.py):
    - the bridge sends the node its welcome and, right after it, a status hint with the same desktop_status, on every node hello (connect or in-band). It then sends the node a status hint whenever voice_active, brain or active_job change, only while the link is on and only on the socket and session whose welcome went out (a new socket or session gets the value again). A voice turn or speech that starts voice_active goes out at once (UI, agent peers and the node); the end of the 60 s voice window goes out within the 1 s status tick;
    - the node merges brain, active_job and desktop_status from welcome and status hints by key (a hint that carries only an alert keeps the earlier values). It trusts desktop_status only from the link session that is connected now, and then either from a status hint (the last pushed value holds until a newer hint replaces it) or, from a welcome alone, for at most 20 s (a snapshot). Anything else is unknown, which counts as voice active (K-73 Mirror);
    - a bridge without this change sends only the welcome, so a new node treats voice as unknown after 20 s and defers large files until the bridge is deployed with it (safe, but they wait).
- exec:
  - fields: call_id, tool or pc.* operation, args, args_sha256, param_schema_sha256, timeout_s, lock_wait_s, start_by, seq, room, origin, approval?;
  - start_by is on the agent clock (send + 2.5 s). The node turns it, with the measured offset, into a monotonic deadline at most 30 s ahead, and past that deadline answers START_WINDOW_MISSED;
  - approval? {confirm_id, channel 'ui'|'voice', risk, args_sha256} is the agent's ConfirmFlow result for a confirm-class call (K-76), inside the signed, encrypted body.
- ack: accepted, risk, cls, code?. accepted:false with a code is a refusal (above): a link, clock or policy code.
- progress: at least every 10 s while running.
