- result: status, K-12 result, duration_ms, effect none|done|possible, blobs[{blob_id, sha256, size, mime}].
  - v8, open REQ-CONTRACT (C-122 departs from this): POST /vortex/desktop/blob answers {blob_id, size} with a blob_id the bridge draws itself (32 hex), which is the id the agent fetches on /internal/blob/<id>, while the chunk AAD id is a separate 32-hex id the node draws (encrypt_blob). So the node's blobs entry is {blob_id (the bridge's fetch id), seal_id (the AAD id), sha256 and size of the plaintext, mime}: one field more than listed above, and the AAD 'blob_id' of the Blobs rule is the seal_id. A pc.* operation returns its blobs as a top-level 'blobs' list of its result, which the node moves into the result body beside the K-12 result. No agent code reads blobs yet. To settle: either the entry gains seal_id here (the agent decrypts with seal_id and fetches with blob_id), or the bridge stores the blob under the node's AAD id.
- result_ack.
- result_resend:
  - a fresh envelope: new id and ts, the current sess, to and session key;
  - the header keeps the call's call_id, tool, room and origin;
  - body {call_id, original_ts, finished_at, result};
  - the agent dedupes it by call_id.
- cancel: answered 'cancelled' within 5 s, or with the real result.
- event (encrypted, to one agent peer):
  - kinds: location | window_context | clipboard_suggestion | log_batch. Any other kind fails when the body is opened;
  - location and log_batch go to the svc peer;
  - window_context and clipboard_suggestion go to the job peer serving the owner room (not svc, not a canary or probe room);
  - with no such peer, the event is dropped;
  - the node sends its current location again after each svc agent_hello, and its current window_context after each owner-room agent_hello.
  - v8 (C-122 sensors as built, src/core/desktop/sensors.py; active run mode only, never with --canary). Every body is built through an exact field allow-list (unknown, missing, null or mistyped fields raise BAD_ARGS and nothing is sent):
    - location {city (text <= 100), lat (-90..90), lng (-180..180), ts, source? 'device'}: looked up at start and every 600 s (60 s after a failed lookup) from ipinfo.io, the PC brain's source, and sent with source 'device'; never a notice and never logged;
    - window_context {title?, ts}: the foreground title read every 5 s and sent only on a change; at most 200 characters, user paths, mail addresses and runs of 7 or more digits masked, non-printable characters replaced and whitespace collapsed; a password manager or a sensitive-path title is sent as 'private window'. A title is never logged at any level;
    - clipboard_suggestion {id, error_excerpt (<= 200, may be empty), query (<= 300), solution (<= 500, may be empty), source_url? (http or https, <= 2048), ts}: from the K-19 ClipboardMonitor, excerpt and query masked as above;
    - window and clipboard sensing pause while the desktop mode is off, the panic latch holds or Windows is locked: no title is read and, on entering the pause, the current window_context is replaced by a title-less one (it clears the agent's cache, so no old title is sent again after an agent_hello); the clipboard monitor is stopped, and on resume the clipboard as it is then counts as already seen.
- notice (node → 'bridge', signed, not encrypted, never relayed):
  - {kind: vitals_pc | desktop_state | power | alert, ...}, with each kind's exact field list (K-74);
  - a missing, unknown, null, mistyped or out-of-range field is refused when building (BAD_ARGS) and at check 8;
  - the bridge uses notices for desktop_status, vitals and alerts.
- control:
  - from the bridge, tighten-only kinds: desktop_stop (→ read), desktop_off, active_job, link_disabled;
  - from an agent (signed): the tighten-only kinds plus stop_all.
- ping/pong:
  - agent↔node every 30 s in both directions, in every node run mode, and once right after each handshake, so that a new session is measured at once;
  - ping body {}; pong body {echo: the ping id, t1: the ping's receive time}; t2 = the pong ts;
  - the pinger registers each ping (id, send time, target) with ClockEstimator.ping_sent(). That is all the wiring a link needs: its Receiver hands every pong it verifies, and the usable ones outside the window, to that estimator (check 5);
  - on a usable pong it computes offset = ((t1 − t0) + (t2 − t3)) / 2, where t3 = t0 + the round trip on the monotonic clock;
  - a new sample replaces the previous one at once, counts for 600 s and ends the re-measure state. A handshake with a hello accepted only on the raw own clock drops it and starts that state (check 5);
  - deadlines use monotonic time.
- sync_request: sent by an agent after it starts.
- Internal operations (never LLM-visible; on an allow-list): pc.ping, pc.capture_screen, pc.capture_webcam, pc.read_file, pc.fetch, pc.open_url, pc.speak_local, pc.play_sound.
  - v8 (C-122 as built, src/core/desktop/capabilities.py; registered in every node run mode, the K-76 policy refuses actuation from canary rooms). Arguments must fit the operation's K-71 schema exactly (no unknown name, every required one, the right type), else a K-12 BAD_ARGS result. While a call runs, the handler sees only its call context (call_id, the agent peer, origin, room, class, risk and the approval reference {confirm_id, channel, risk}), never logged:
    - pc.capture_screen: the primary monitor; pc.capture_webcam: one frame (the last good one of 5 reads, since the first frames of many cameras are dark); both JPEG, longest side at most 1600 px, quality 78, uploaded as a blob (K-73). The K-76 capture rule (password manager or sensitive-path title in front) is judged again right before the pixels are taken (SENSITIVE_SCREEN);
    - pc.read_file: only with the approval reference it was accepted with (else APPROVAL_REQUIRED); the path is resolved again through the K-76 path policy (PATH_NOT_ALLOWED), a regular file of at most 25 MB (FILE_TOO_LARGE), uploaded as a blob, and audited as read_file_exposed (call_id, confirm_id, channel, byte count; never the path);
    - pc.fetch: K-73 pc.fetch through the mirror (below); pc.open_url: one http or https URL with a host and no user info, at most 2048 printable characters without whitespace, in the default browser; pc.speak_local: at most 1000 printable characters, a system notice sound first; pc.play_sound: name startup | chime | notify | alert (notify and alert are Windows system sounds);
    - a blob is sealed to the session key of the agent peer that sent the call and charged to the K-76 uploads cap before the PC-signed upload (DESKTOP_RATE_LIMITED, UPLOAD_FAILED);
    - the startup sound plays once per supervisor start and Windows boot, in active mode only and never while JARVIS_TEST_MODE is 1/true/yes/on;
    - nothing here logs an argument, a path, a URL, a title or a spoken text.

Semantics and timers
- At most once. call_id is the idempotency key. Retries happen only for the read class.
- Timers:
  - presence:
    - the bridge counts every verified node message except ping and pong, because the probes skip check 5 at the bridge;
    - the node's link (C-120) sends a desktop_state notice every 10 s, in every run mode (active and --canary) and every desktop mode, whatever its sensors do;
    - the node is stale after 25 s without a counted message;
  - ack 3 s, then cancel plus a 2 s grace;
  - stall 30 s without progress → cancel → DESKTOP_TIMEOUT;
  - proxy cap = 3 + lock_wait + timeout + 10 s;
  - outbox 10 min / 200 entries.
- Dead-man switch: a link down for more than 5 s cancels running input-class calls; a messaging send step completes atomically.
- Known gap (v7, open REQ-CONTRACT): the node's 5 s timer starts only when its Socket.IO client reports the link disconnected (or suspended). A clean close is seen at once, but a silent loss (a dropped network with no close) is seen only through the Engine.IO heartbeat, and the bridge's socketio.AsyncServer (src/core/ui_bridge.py, which also carries '/desktop') sets no ping values, so python-engineio's defaults apply: ping_interval 25 s and ping_timeout 20 s. A silent loss is therefore detected after about 25 to 50 s, not the 5 s this contract states, and the node's link sets no faster heartbeat of its own (its K-70 ping to the agent peers is every 30 s and does not end the connection). The planned fix is a ping of about 5 s on the '/desktop' namespace or a node-level ping that ends the connection when it goes unanswered (C-116/C-117 follow-up); until it lands, the 5 s figure holds only for a link loss the client notices.
- Outcomes:
  - 'Not executed' (DESKTOP_NOT_STARTED) only after a refusal coded DESKTOP_REJECTED or START_WINDOW_MISSED (above), a tombstone or start_window_missed, or when the bridge reports dl_undeliverable{emitted:false}. A refusal with another code returns that code.
  - A laptop that is offline before sending gives DESKTOP_OFFLINE.
  - Every other loss gives DESKTOP_RESULT_UNKNOWN, reconciled on hello or sync_request. Late outcomes are announced, and the tool_sync end is corrected under the same id.

Versioning
- The highest version common to both proto lists is used; none in common gives PROTO_MISMATCH.
- Rolling order: bridge → agent → node.

Logging
- The bridge logs only call_id, tool, sizes and timings, never arguments, results, window titles or notice bodies.
- Link errors carry a reason and a code, never message content, keys or plaintext.

Rates (message rates, not CPU/RAM limits)
- exec 10/s burst and 120/min; events and notices 20/s; connects 10/min per IP.
- Only failed verifications count toward the per-IP limit. An authentic message refused only as stale or future is not a failed verification.
- v42 (C-119 as built, services/ai_core/desktop_link.py: the agent end):
  - Process and transport:
    - one DesktopLink per process, on its own event loop in a daemon thread; every public method is thread-safe and never blocks;
    - built at the first remote-mode session (desktop_proxy.attach_session -> ensure_link) as peer 'job-<room>' ('svc' for jarvis-agent-svc, K-77), from DESKTOP_AGENT_SIGNING_KEY and DESKTOP_PC_PUBLIC_KEY;
    - without usable keys (logged once, names only) or with a seen store that cannot open, there is no link, and laptop calls answer DESKTOP_OFFLINE;
    - '/desktop' on UI_BRIDGE_URL, websocket only, through the node's SocketIOTransport;
    - reconnection=False with its own loop: 1 -> 30 s doubling plus up to 1 s jitter, forever, back to 1 s after a connection that lasted 60 s;
    - the signed agent_hello goes in the connect auth on every connect.
  - Handshake:
    - the connect agent_hello names no session; the session key comes from the node's hello to this peer;
    - a hello of a new node session gets an in-band agent_hello that names it, with a new ephemeral key;
    - node sessions are told apart by arrival, never by the node's ts; a hello of a session this link replaced less than 120 s ago is ignored (a relay may reorder hellos);
    - after each handshake, in order: the hello's WAL report, a pending desktop_stop, a ping, the process's first sync_request, the waiting controls.
  - Calls: CallRequest {tool, args, param_schema_sha256, timeout_s, lock_wait_s, origin, seq?, approval?, call_id, label, budget_s?, speech_id?}, kept in a pending map (never sio.call).
    - Calls are sent one at a time, in the order they were submitted: a FIFO lock is taken first and held until the exec went out.
    - Answered at once, nothing sent:
      - CLOCK_SKEW while skew_exceeded(), checked before the offline check;
      - STOPPED_BY_USER for 3 s after a stop;
      - DESKTOP_OFFLINE without a node session, or while a desktop_status newer than the session's hello says offline;
      - DESKTOP_NOT_STARTED for a call_id in flight, for one first sent more than 1 h ago (first-send times are kept 24 h), or when budget_s leaves less than the ack window plus the grace, with a 1 s margin;
      - BAD_ARGS when the exec cannot be built.
    - A pending desktop_stop not yet sent in this session, and a stop_all that waited, go out before the exec.
    - seq: a request that names its speech (speech_id, the seq speech_id form) and has no seq of its own gets {speech_id, n} right before its exec is built. n counts the execs of that speech this link sent, from 0; the last 256 speeches are remembered. A call answered without a send (any case above, a failed send answered DESKTOP_OFFLINE, or a cancelled send) gives its number back, so the node's SeqGate never holds the speech's next call for a number no exec carries. A request with its own seq keeps it. The exec carries seq only when one was stamped.
  - Outcomes:
    - no ack in 3 s: cancel, 2 s grace, DESKTOP_RESULT_UNKNOWN;
    - 30 s without progress: cancel, DESKTOP_TIMEOUT (also when the node answers that cancel with cancelled or not_started);
    - the whole call, cancel and grace included, ends 1 s before the proxy cap and before budget_s runs out (budget_s is what is left of the caller's K-11 timeout);
    - DESKTOP_NOT_STARTED after a refusal coded DESKTOP_REJECTED or START_WINDOW_MISSED, a never_started or start_window_missed WAL report, a not_started/effect-none answer to the ack-window cancel, or dl_undeliverable {emitted:false};
    - every other refusal code is returned as it is;
    - a WAL 'interrupted' gives DESKTOP_RESULT_UNKNOWN;
    - a node result with any status but 'completed' and effect 'possible' is DESKTOP_RESULT_UNKNOWN for the model and Sir; the node's status, code and message stay only in data (laptop_status, laptop_error_code, laptop_message);
    - every other loss gives DESKTOP_RESULT_UNKNOWN;
    - a laptop code counts only in the K-12 form [A-Z0-9_]{1,64}: a refusal with any other code is DESKTOP_REJECTED, and any other result error_code is not taken as the outcome's code;
    - an event that lands as its wait runs out is still handled, and a result queued behind a stop or a link loss is the call's outcome.
  - Reconciliation:
    - an unknown, timed-out or stopped call stays open for 1 h;
    - its later result or result_resend, a WAL report (never_started or start_window_missed -> not_started; interrupted), or a refusal ack goes once to the 'late' listeners as LateOutcome {call_id, tool, reason: unknown|timeout|stopped|restart|delivery, state: result|not_started|interrupted|completed, result?, status?, effect?, label};
    - a WAL 'completed' without its result_resend within 15 s is handed on as 'completed': an end whose outcome is not known;
    - every result gets a result_ack and is deduped by call_id in the seen store (24 h), except one proving its call never ran (not_started, effect none), because the same call_id may still run after an approval;
    - a new result of a call this process never waited for goes on once, with reason 'restart'.
  - Stops:
    - stop_all(reason, desktop_stop=False) refuses new calls for 3 s, ends every call in flight STOPPED_BY_USER (kept open), and sends the agent-signed control stop_all whenever a call of this peer may still run: one in flight, or one still open that no result or WAL report has ended;
    - without a session, that stop_all waits for the next handshake, goes before that session's first exec, and is dropped when the hello's WAL report shows nothing left to stop;
    - a status hint with stop_all: true does the same.
  - desktop_stop:
    - the agent-signed control desktop_stop is sent only while the laptop is online; otherwise it goes first at the laptop's next hello, before any exec;
    - it stays pending until the laptop reports mode read or off (a hello, or a status hint of the online laptop), and is re-sent at every new hello until then;
    - it is kept in conversations/desktop_stop.json (written atomically, file-locked, shared by the agent processes; an unreadable file counts as pending), so a later agent process sends it;
    - the file goes once the laptop reported read or off; a stop kept after that report stays;
    - desktop_stop_persisted is False when the file could not be written: the stop then holds only for this process;
    - a desktop_stop said while the current session's desktop_status already shows the laptop online in read or off is done once it is sent. Nothing stays pending or on disk, so it never goes out again at a later hello and never undoes a tray Full.
  - Origins: each exec carries its request's own origin: 'llm' for the model's calls and 'job' for a VPS job's laptop re-run (K-71), 'internal' for jarvis_delivery. Any of them becomes 'canary' in a K-57 probe or canary room (jarvis-probe-<n>, jarvis-canary-<n>).
  - jarvis_delivery's DesktopSender (C-113): online(), and submit(op, args) for pc.fetch and pc.open_url with exactly their PC_OPERATIONS fields. Errors: DeliveryError BAD_ARGS for anything else, DESKTOP_OFFLINE when offline, DELIVERY_FAILED for any other fast refusal. An end other than success reaches the 'late' listeners (reason 'delivery'); a delivery kept open is reported only by its late outcome.
  - End of a job: retire(link) closes the link for good, from any thread and without waiting. agent_runner calls it through desktop_proxy.end_job when a remote-mode job ends, also on cancel, and at once when LiveKit shuts the job down. A retired link never reconnects as the room's peer (the bridge keeps one socket per peer), a call in flight ends DESKTOP_RESULT_UNKNOWN, and the link is forgotten as the process's link and delivery sender, so a later job of the process builds its own.
  - Laptop state comes only from welcome and status hints (agents get no notices). Logs carry call ids, tools, codes and timings, never arguments, results or keys.

#### K-71 · DESKTOP-MANIFEST + PLACEMENT (file-format+python-api) · owner: Claude
Manifest file
- services/ai_core/desktop_manifest.json is generated on Windows by scripts/desktop/export_manifest.py (JARVIS_TEST_MODE=true, dead bridge URL) from the committed tree, and baked into the agent image.
- The node runs the same git SHA from a pinned snapshot and uses its live registry.
- Top level: {version, git_sha, manifest_sha256}.
- Per tool:
  - name, module, doc (exact __doc__);
  - params [{name, kind, annotation, default, required}];
  - meta {timeout, risk 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'dynamic', arg_policies, exclusive, voice_confirm, max_output_chars, long_running};
  - cls, placement, idempotent;
  - param_schema_sha256 (names, annotations, required only);
  - lk_schema_sha256 (the full LLM declaration).
- pc.* operation schemas are listed too.
- Annotation whitelist: str, int, float, bool, None, X | None, list[str|int], dict[str,str], Literal[str…]. Anything else fails the export.

Placement table
- services/ai_core/tool_placement.py, per tool: place 'vps'|'laptop'|'split'|route(args, presence), fallback, fallback_on [codes], idempotent, cls floor, arg_hooks, opens_urls, timeout_override.
- JARVIS_TOOL_PLACEMENT_OVERRIDES='name=laptop,…' is validated: GUI tools never vps, wrap_* never laptop, laptop only for manifest tools. It applies from the next session.
- PC brain mode ignores the table.
- VPS argument hooks (v7, C-124 as built): in remote mode services/ai_core/remote_compat.install_arg_hooks wraps, after discovery and before the tools are converted for LiveKit, every tool that has an arg_hook whose side is 'vps' (tool_placement.ARG_HOOKS), and applies it to the bound arguments before each call. A routed call that goes to the laptop gets no VPS hook; the PC brain installs none.
  - vps_attachment (send_email attachment_path): the realpath must lie inside /app/Jarvis_Outputs, /app/Jarvis_Shared, the configured outputs and shared folders or the agent's blob dir (K-73), and in no denied tree: /proc, /sys, /etc, and conversations, chroma_db, data, logs, backups, .env, .env.agent and .env.svc under /app and under the project root. A relative path is tried against the project root and the outputs folder. The checked realpath is what the tool gets.
  - vps_media_path (zip_files folder_path on the VPS): the same deny list, strictly inside the media folders.
  - safe_name (download_images folder_name, generate_qr_code filename, zip_files zip_name): reduced to its basename ('\\' counts as a separator, a drive prefix is dropped); '', '.' or '..' drops the argument so the tool's default applies.
  - owner_recipient (send_email and autonomous_research_and_email recipient): a recipient other than the owner raises the call to K-45 HIGH (K-45 v7).
  - A refused path returns the K-12 error {status:'error', error_code: ARG_PATH_DENIED | ARG_PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOTS | ARG_INVALID} and the tool never runs; the argument value is never in the message.

VPS discovery (JARVIS_DESKTOP_MODE=remote)
- Skip modules whose tools are all laptop-placed, plus the static deny-list: keyboard_mouse_ctrl, jarvis_window_ctrl, jarvis_whatsapp_automation, jarvis_notepad_automation, jarvis_system_ctrl, jarvis_system_info, jarvis_browser_pinchtab.
- Laptop-placed tools in imported modules are swapped for proxies, and proxies are added for the remaining manifest tools.
- Expected names = discovery ∪ manifest (never a constant). A mismatch logs ERROR and sets module_health degraded.
- Counts on 2026-10-01: 83 names = vps 32 (including confirm_action and the 4 internal wrap_* tools), split 1 (analyze_screen), routed 2 (zip_files, list_generated_media_tool), laptop 48. v18 (C-57, 08 Oct): 85 names = vps 34 (+ list_background_jobs, cancel_background_job), split 1, routed 2, laptop 48. v20 (X-29, 08 Oct): 86 names = vps 34, split 1, routed 2, laptop 49 (+ cancel_shutdown, class de_escalation, so it never needs an approval); the manifest lists 82 tools. v21 (X-32, 08 Oct): 87 names = vps 35 (+ cancel_scheduled_task, beside schedule_task and list_tasks), split 1, routed 2, laptop 49; the manifest lists 83 tools. v23 (X-43, 08 Oct): 88 names = vps 35, split 1, routed 2, laptop 50 (+ close_window, class input like close); the manifest lists 84 tools.

Proxies
- Built in prewarm with the same __name__, __qualname__, __module__, __doc__ and __signature__ (real type objects, nothing eval'd).
- Registered once per process (the C-32 prewarm) through register_tool, never through update_tools. Settings: exclusive None, retry_attempts 0, timeout = the K-70 link cap.
- Link errors are returned as K-12 dicts and never count as circuit-breaker failures.
- Repeat guard: the same messaging, code_exec, availability, exposure or typing call (same args_sha256) within 120 s needs ConfirmFlow.
- seq is stamped by the agent's link right before it builds the exec (v42); only an exec that is sent takes a number.

Drift
- At exec time the node compares param_schema_sha256: a mismatch gives MANIFEST_MISMATCH and the tool does not run. A docstring-only drift logs WARNING.
- A manifest sent by the node is never adopted at runtime.
- The deploy pre-flight and CI run with JARVIS_MANIFEST_STRICT=1 and refuse a stale committed manifest. tests/unit/test_desktop_manifest.py is advisory otherwise.
- Fallback: a VPS result with a code in fallback_on and effect none gets one re-run on the laptop. VPS runs of that tool then back off for 6 h.
v34 (C-81, as built): start_swarm_mode is placed 'vps' (not idempotent). 89 names = vps 36, split 1, routed 2, laptop 50; the manifest lists 85 tools.
v42 (C-119, as built, services/ai_core/desktop_proxy.py):
- install(plugin_manager): runs in the C-32 prewarm and on its PREWARM_MISS path, right after discovery and before the VPS argument hooks and the LiveKit conversion; remote mode only.
  - Every laptop-placed tool of the committed manifest becomes a proxy (placements are taken after the validated JARVIS_TOOL_PLACEMENT_OVERRIDES). The proxy has the manifest's __name__, __qualname__, __module__, __doc__ and __signature__, with real types from the annotation whitelist.
  - It is registered once through register_tool:
    - exclusive None, retry_attempts 0;
    - timeout = the link cap. The tool's own timeout is the placement's timeout_override, else the manifest's, else 15 s; lock_wait is 30 s for every K-16 desktop_input tool;
    - the manifest's arg_policies, max_output_chars and long_running;
    - risk = the static risk floor;
    - confirm_summary = the laptop summary (K-76), prefixed with 'dobara karun?' when the same call was sent within the repeat window.
  - A laptop tool that an imported module registered is swapped for its proxy. A second install changes nothing, and update_tools is never called.
  - A param_schema_sha256 mismatch logs ERROR (the proxy follows the manifest). An lk_schema drift logs WARNING (not compared across library versions). A laptop tool missing from the manifest logs ERROR.
- Routed tools (zip_files, list_generated_media_tool) and VPS tools with a laptop fallback (today download_youtube_media, fallback_on YT_BOT_CHECK) get one K-11 dispatcher.
  - Per call, a routed tool's route (with the link's online state) or the fallback back-off decides where it runs.
  - A call that goes to the laptop is asked with the laptop summary; one that stays on the VPS keeps the tool's own summary.
  - K-11 timeout: max(VPS, cap) for a routed tool, VPS + cap for a fallback tool.
  - Every proxy and dispatcher carries __jarvis_desktop__ (name, class, route). The K-11 wrapper takes from it tool_sync source 'desktop' (K-13 v4) and create_pending(desktop=True, desktop_class) (K-14 v42).
- A call:
  - the K-11 checks run first; the static risk floor is asked before anything is sent (the class floor: code_exec high; messaging, availability and exposure medium; plus the manifest's fixed risk and K-45 through the wrapper);
  - the exec carries the approval reference only for the approved run's own unused approval of this tool and these arguments. With another tool's approval it carries none, so the node asks; with other arguments the answer is APPROVAL_INVALID and nothing is sent;
  - the link gets what is left of the K-11 timeout (plugin_manager.tool_time_left) as budget_s;
  - every link outcome is a K-12 dict, never an exception and never a breaker failure;
  - the laptop call is never cancelled with its caller;
  - each call writes one DESKTOP_CALL line to logs/security.log (TOOL, CALL, OUTCOME, CODE in the K-12 form only), never arguments.
- APPROVAL_REQUIRED from the node (an ack refusal, or the not_started/effect-none result of its pre-run re-check) becomes a desktop ConfirmFlow item at high. Its approval re-sends the exec under the same call_id, with no seq and no budget. An approval below what the node then needs is asked again at high.
- Repeat guard: the same (tool, args_sha256) within 120 s of a send asks first ('dobara karun?', at least medium). It covers messaging, code_exec, availability and exposure tools, type_text_tool and type_code_animation_tool. A send is recorded right before it goes out, so a parallel call or a retry after a cancelled wait sees it; only an outcome proving the call never ran takes it back.
- Ordering: the proxy submits the call to the link synchronously in its first step, before its first await, naming its LiveKit speech (CallRequest.speech_id; none when the id is not of the seq speech_id form). The link stamps seq right before it builds the exec (K-70 v42), so only an exec that is sent takes a number. A call answered in the proxy (a fast refusal, the repeat guard's question, APPROVAL_INVALID, BAD_ARGS) never reaches the link. Approved re-sends, the synchronous fallback and a VPS job's re-run carry no seq.
- Lost outputs and late outcomes:
  - a completed LLM call whose output did not reach function_tools_executed is announced (result shown, a fixed line spoken). It is checked 2 s after the call ended, then every second while its speech still runs, for at most 120 s;
  - a late outcome of an unknown, timed-out or stopped call is announced, and its tool_sync end is corrected under its K-13 id;
  - a stopped call whose late result shows it ended before the stop is announced as done only when that K-12 result says success or started;
  - a WAL 'completed' without a result is announced as ended with its result unknown (the row ends error, DESKTOP_RESULT_UNKNOWN);
  - a delivery failure names only a K-12 code and is spoken as a fixed line; a delivery that may have opened is never called a failure.
- Fallback:
  - a VPS result with a code in fallback_on and effect none (top level and data) gets one re-run on the laptop inside the same LLM call, with origin 'llm';
  - VPS runs of that tool then back off for 6 h, kept in conversations/desktop_backoff.json (file-locked, shared by the agent processes; a write that fails keeps the back-off in memory);
  - a VPS run that started a K-20 job (status 'started' with its job_id) gets the same check on the job's final result, through jarvis_jobs.on_job_end;
  - that job's re-run has origin 'job' (no LLM turn waits for it; K-76 D21). It carries no approval, K-13 id, budget or seq, and its outcome is announced as what the laptop did: ran there, waits for an Allow, outcome not known yet, or could not run there either.
- Per job (agent_runner, remote mode):
  - attach_session runs after every session start. It wires the process's link, the link's late and event listeners on the job's loop, the stop phrases on final voice transcripts and as the router's typed hook, function_tools_executed, and the dashboard Stop (chained once);
  - node window_context events reach assistant.vision_handler.on_window_context({title, ts}) (C-112);
  - end_job, called as the job ends, retires the link once no other job of the process uses it; a late session start of an ended job builds no link.

#### K-72 · BRAIN-SWITCH + PLACEMENT-ENV + COMPAT (env+process) · owner: Claude
Brain switch
- JARVIS_BRAIN=vps|pc in the VPS deploy/hostinger/.env (mode 600) is the source of truth. Compose reads it as ${JARVIS_BRAIN:?}, so a missing value fails fast.
- COMPOSE_PROFILES is derived from it (vps-brain or empty).
- Only scripts/agent_ctl.py brain vps|pc [--when-idle|--now] writes it:
  - states PREFLIGHT → BACKUP → STOP_OLD → SYNC_DATA → FLIP_ENV → START_NEW → ENSURE → VERIFY → DONE;
  - a journal in run/brain_switch.json makes it resumable; a failure restores the previous brain automatically;
  - success is declared only when /vortex/status shows the brain and an agent participant whose lk.agent.name equals the target and whose jarvis.session is running;
  - env writers edit in place and keep unknown lines.
- Idle = no final transcript, typed chat or tool call for 10 min (bridge last_activity_ts). --now gives a spoken 60 s notice.

Agent names
- 'jarvis' (VPS containers) and 'jarvis-pc' (PC fallback, JARVIS_PC_AGENT_NAME in the VPS .env).
- The bridge dispatches only to the active brain.
- In vps mode agent_ctl refuses to start a PC worker. In pc mode the agent and agent-svc are stopped and stay stopped (unless-stopped).

Roles and modes
- JARVIS_ROLE = agent | svc | bridge | desktop.
- JARVIS_DESKTOP_MODE = remote (VPS) | local (PC brain).
- config.validate(role, mode) requires only what that pair uses: agent+remote needs JARVIS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (fatal) and DESKTOP_AGENT_SIGNING_KEY; agent+local needs today's set.

Env names
- Placement and link: JARVIS_TOOL_PLACEMENT_OVERRIDES, JARVIS_LINK_URL (node, https only).
- Node policy: JARVIS_PRESENCE_WINDOW_S=600, JARVIS_CAPTURE_PRESENCE_S=120, JARVIS_ORIGIN_PRESENCE_GATE=0 (D21, K-76 Origins) and the K-15 kill switch JARVIS_DESKTOP_CONTROL. The node starts in mode full and has no laptop-side approval setting (user decision D3).
- Node settings source: the node runs from a read-only snapshot and makes dotenv a no-op, so an allow-listed parser (src/core/desktop/settings.py) reads only non-secret keys from the PC root .env, at start and again when the file changes: JARVIS_DESKTOP_CONTROL, JARVIS_CLIPBOARD_HELPER, JARVIS_CLIPBOARD_SPEAK, JARVIS_LINK_URL, the node policy keys above, WHATSAPP_TEST_NUMBERS and the K-15 path and app keys. Relative paths resolve against JARVIS_DATA_ROOT. PINCHTAB_TOKEN and CONTROLLER_TOKEN stay DPAPI-wrapped in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JARVIS\node and reach config in memory only.
- Node data root: JARVIS_DATA_ROOT (the repo on the PC) and JARVIS_RUN_DIR (<data root>\run), set by the supervisor from %LOCALAPPDATA%\JARVIS\node\node_config.json (written by agent_ctl node update). run/, logs/ and Jarvis_Outputs are the repo's own, and run/desktop_actor.lock is the same file the PC brain takes.
- Worker and session: JARVIS_IDLE_PROCS (VPS 2, PC 1), JARVIS_PREWARM_TIMEOUT=120, JARVIS_LOAD_THRESHOLD=inf, JARVIS_JOB_MEMORY_WARN_MB=3000, JARVIS_SHUTDOWN_PROC_TIMEOUT=20, JARVIS_IDLE_CLOSE_MIN=30, JARVIS_CTX_TRIGGER_TOKENS=24000.
- Dispatch: AGENT_DISPATCH_MODE (on_demand in vps mode).
- Media and network: JARVIS_MEDIA_PRIORITY=normal|low, JARVIS_NET_GUARD (v7: VPS agent/svc only; default off, 1, true, yes or on turns the egress guard on; the compose files do not set it yet, open item) with JARVIS_NET_GUARD_SUBNETS, JARVIS_NET_GUARD_GATEWAYS, JARVIS_NET_GUARD_PUBLIC_IPS (replaces the built-in VPS public IP) and JARVIS_NET_GUARD_ALLOW_HOSTS.
- Room input: JARVIS_RPC_OWNER_ONLY (v7: PC brain only, default off; always on in remote mode, K-56 v7). Room watchdog: JARVIS_ROOM_WATCHDOG (v7: default on, pc mode only, K-53 v7).
- Reminders and backups: JARVIS_REMINDER_EMAIL_AFTER_MIN=0, BACKUP_RECIPIENT_PUBLIC_KEY.
- Identity and time: TZ=Asia/Karachi, USER_CITY, JARVIS_USER_ID (every mode).
- Manifest: JARVIS_MANIFEST_STRICT (deploy/CI).

Compat layer
- services/ai_core/remote_compat.py is active only when JARVIS_DESKTOP_MODE=remote and installed before discovery:
  - os.startfile → services.utils.jarvis_delivery.open_artifact (raises OSError('DESKTOP_OFFLINE') when the laptop is offline);
  - webbrowser.open → pc.open_url, only inside a tool flagged opens_urls and only for http(s) URLs;
  - jarvis_search.get_current_city / get_current_city_data and every by-value consumer → services.utils.jarvis_location (device location cache, else USER_CITY; never ipinfo).
- A startup self-test asserts every patched symbol; a missing one logs ERROR COMPAT_SHIM_MISSING and degrades module_health.
- Cursor replaces the shims with hooks (X-64, X-65). The shimmed symbols are frozen until then.

Process hardening (v7, C-124 as built: services/utils/net_guard.py)
- harden_process() runs at import of src/core/agent_runner.py (the worker and every job process) and again in the job entrypoint. It acts only in a Linux agent or svc process of the VPS brain (remote mode, JARVIS_BRAIN=vps or a container); the PC worker on Windows gets nothing.
- Child processes: every subprocess.Popen (so every asyncio subprocess) gets an environment allow-list (PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_*, TZ, TMPDIR, HF_* without tokens, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE). An explicit env keeps only those names plus names the caller added that the parent does not have and that do not look like a secret; a parent name outside the list is dropped whatever its value.
- prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) makes the process non-dumpable (set again on every call, because an exec resets it).
- Egress guard, only with JARVIS_NET_GUARD on: socket.create_connection and socket.connect/connect_ex for AF_INET/AF_INET6 refuse loopback, RFC 1918, CGNAT, link-local (169.254.169.254 included), ULA, multicast, 0.0.0.0/8 and every other non-global address, also in IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 and 6to4 spellings, plus the Docker gateway and the VPS public IP. The jarvis-network subnet is allowed except its gateway, network and broadcast addresses. A host name is resolved by the guard (cached at most 30 s) and the vetted address is what the socket connects to. It is best effort against SSRF only: subprocesses, C extensions with their own sockets (LiveKit's Rust core, gRPC) and raw sendto() are not covered.
- 'python -m services.utils.net_guard --self-test' is the deploy gate's check (K-75): the bridge, LiveKit and Gemini must be allowed; the Docker gateway, the public IP and the forbidden ranges refused.
- Settings names only, values never logged; one PROCESS_HARDENING log line records what was applied.
v9 (C-23): the bridge's dispatch target follows K-44 v9: vps mode its JARVIS_AGENT_NAME ('jarvis'); pc mode the name the PC worker reports (ensure body) or was last seen with, from {'', JARVIS_PC_AGENT_NAME}. The PC worker registers JARVIS_AGENT_NAME from the PC root .env: unset ('') until C-23 phase 3, then jarvis-pc, which VERIFY needs. The bridge reads JARVIS_BRAIN when it starts, so a switch recreates ui-bridge after FLIP_ENV and before ENSURE (C-126).
v36 (C-126, as built): JARVIS_MEDIA_PRIORITY (non-secret; the media wrappers read it) joins the child-env allow-list. The compose file sets JARVIS_NET_GUARD=1 for agent and agent-svc (the v7 open item is closed). harden_process() runs in PID 1 of both agent containers (no init). agent_ctl's brain switch recreates ui-bridge alone at START_NEW (up -d --no-deps --no-build --pull never --force-recreate ui-bridge, GIT_SHA from the running bridge container, else the first line of DEPLOYED_SHA) and waits up to 120 s for Docker's healthy, in both directions; a restore after START_NEW began recreates it again; every agent_ctl 'up' uses --no-deps --no-build --pull never.
v40 (C-114, as built): JARVIS_IDLE_CLOSE_MIN=30 and JARVIS_CTX_TRIGGER_TOKENS=24000 are the defaults the VPS agent applies when the names are empty, so compose need not set them; in pc mode JARVIS_IDLE_CLOSE_MIN defaults to off (K-69 v40).
v41 (C-127, as built):
- config.validate('bridge') (C-112; V2a ships it while the env files stay unchanged) needs LIVEKIT_API_KEY and LIVEKIT_API_SECRET and, while the legacy token is in use (LEGACY_TOKEN_AUTH unset or true), VORTEX_SECURITY_TOKEN; never an AI key. AGENT_TOKEN and BRIDGE_HMAC_SECRET stay optional.
- 'agent_ctl brain vps', once the Desktop Node has started, wraps the PC fallback secrets (K-47 v41) from the root .env and deploy/windows-local/.env into run/fallback.env.dpapi. It is refused (a warning only; the secrets stay in the env files) while the laptop's JARVIS_BRAIN is not vps, a PC worker holds run/agent.lock, or a PC copy of a VPS env file in the repo (deploy/hostinger/.env, bridge.env, .env.agent) holds a fallback secret or cannot be read.
- 'agent_ctl brain pc' unwraps them back into the env files just before it starts the PC worker. A 'brain pc' that starts nothing (already pc, or --laptop-only) does it at its end; audit field fallback_secrets: restored | failed | 'kept (the Desktop Node runs)'.
- Never while the Desktop Node runs: then no worker starts and the store is kept (exit 4 for a 'brain pc' that would start nothing). A failed restore keeps the store and the env files as they were and starts no worker; its output names the way out for a store this Windows user cannot use.
- While run/fallback.env.dpapi exists, every PC worker start (start, restart) is refused with exit 4. The refusal names 'brain pc' and, for a store this Windows user can never unwrap, 'scripts/ops/fallback_env.py --discard --confirm'.
- The live JARVIS_BRAIN and COMPOSE_PROFILES lines survive every rollback: rollback.sh --with-env writes them back into a restored .env (K-75 v41).

#### K-73 · MEDIA-RELAY + FILES + BLOBS (http-api) · owner: Claude
Scope
- This is the single media path (it fills DASH-C21 and DASH-C30). The UI and the laptop node both use it; no second file endpoint exists.

Media relay
- The bridge mounts jarvis_shared and jarvis_outputs read-only and serves:
  - GET /vortex/media/index?area=shared|outputs&cursor=<ts>;
  - GET /vortex/media/file?area=&path= (HTTP Range).
- Auth: the owner session (the legacy token until C-22) for the UI, or K-70 PC-signed HTTP for the node.
- Allowed paths:
  - shared: Generated_Images/, QR_Codes/, Downloads/ (including YouTube/);
  - outputs: Downloads/, leads/ and top-level *.zip.
- Excluded: sim_lookup_history.jsonl, dotfiles, *.part, *.ytdl, *.tmp, and files modified less than 5 s ago.
  - v7 (C-117 as built): a dotfile is any path component that starts with '.', so a file inside a dot-directory (for example Downloads/.cache/x.bin) is excluded too. Such a relpath is never walked into, listed, opened or served, also not for a Range request.
- Files are opened component by component with O_NOFOLLOW (directories via dir_fd and O_DIRECTORY). Only regular files are served; symlinks are never listed or streamed.
  - v7 (C-117 as built): on POSIX this dir_fd + O_NOFOLLOW walk is mandatory. A POSIX build without dir_fd (or without O_NOFOLLOW/O_DIRECTORY) answers every media request with 503 {error:'platform'} and never falls back. The lexical + realpath fallback (it refuses symlinks, without the race guard) exists only on Windows, where the module is imported for its tests.
- Index entries: {seq, relpath, size, mtime_ns, sha256?}. The node's cursor is the listing time − 5 s, with dedupe by relpath+size+mtime and a full reconcile every 15 min.

Mirror (node)
- Additive only, never deletes, into config.shared_dir and config.outputs_dir.
- Every relpath component is validated: no '\\', ':', '..', control characters, CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9, or trailing dot or space.
- Joined with safe_child_path; the final realpath must stay under the root.
- Write order: .part → size check (plus sha256 when known) → Mark-of-the-Web (ZoneId=3) → rename without following reparse points. A clash gets a ' (n)' suffix.
- Files over 20 MB are copied only while desktop_status.voice_active is false, or on an explicit open.
- v8 (C-122 as built, src/core/desktop/mirror.py; an active-mode node task, never with --canary):
  - Polling: GET /media/index per area every 20 s (PC-signed, TLS verified, https only), with the cursor the bridge returns; a full listing of the area every 15 min. A file that could not be copied (an error, the byte cap, a deferred large file) holds the cursor below its mtime, so no file is skipped; a repeated failure of one file backs off 60 s doubling to 1 h (in memory).
  - Names: besides the rules above, no character Windows refuses in a name, no dotfile, COM0-9 and LPT0-9 (also with superscript digits) and CONIN$/CONOUT$/CLOCK$ as device names (also with an extension), at most 255 bytes per component, at most 16 directory levels, and only the K-73 subtrees of the area. Names Explorer parses while browsing are refused: desktop.ini, autorun.inf, folder.htt and the suffixes .url, .lnk, .library-ms, .searchconnector-ms, .search-ms, .scf, .website, .theme, .themepack, .deskthemepack, .appref-ms, .pif. A refused name is audited once per relpath + size + mtime and never logged.
  - Refused once and for good (audited; it never holds the cursor and is never charged): a name or path too long for the disk, a target in the K-76 sensitive set (the outputs folder allowed), a file over 8 GiB or over the whole deliveries cap. The K-76 deliveries cap is charged only after every folder, name and sensitive check, right before the download; a cap trip holds that file and every larger one for the rest of the pass (smaller ones are still tried, a second trip ends the pass), then the mirror pauses 10 min, doubling on each pass with a trip up to 6 h.
  - Write order: '<name>.<random>.part' in the target folder, size check and sha256 check (when known), Mark-of-the-Web, then a rename that never overwrites and never follows a reparse point; a folder in the chain that is a link or reparse point refuses the file.
  - voice_active: the value the node trusts under K-70 v8 (Bridge hints); unknown counts as active, so a file over 20 MB waits unless opened, and the mirror logs that once per unknown spell (INFO, no names).
- pc.fetch v8 (as built): sha256 is 64 lowercase hex and size >= 0 (else BAD_ARGS); a refused name is BAD_ARGS, a cap trip DESKTOP_RATE_LIMITED, every other failure DELIVERY_FAILED with a short spoken reason, including 'deferred_voice_active' and, while voice is unknown, 'deferred_voice_unknown' for a file over 20 MB fetched without open. With open, an auto-open type is opened with its default handler and any other file is only selected in Explorer (OPEN_FAILED if that fails). The result names the copy below its area root (it may differ by ' (n)'), never the absolute local path; the delivery is audited as fetch_delivered (saved, opened or revealed).

pc.fetch
- Body: {area, relpath, sha256 (agent-signed, required), size, open}.
- Auto-open only for audio, video, image, pdf, txt, csv, json, xlsx, docx, pptx and html. Executables, scripts, shortcuts and archives are never opened; Explorer selects them instead.
- open_artifact raises OSError('DESKTOP_OFFLINE') while the laptop is offline, so tools report the truth. Opens that finish later are announced.

Blobs (laptop → VPS)
- POST /vortex/desktop/blob. nginx allows client_max_body_size 30m on this location only, with request buffering off.
- The signed headers (length ≤ 30 MB and sha256) are verified before the body is read.
- The body is streamed and hashed under a hard cap, with at most 2 concurrent uploads.
- Storage: in-memory only, ≤ 256 MB in total, TTL 15 min, deleted after the first fetch.
- The body is AEAD-encrypted to the agent session.
- The agent fetches GET /internal/blob/<id> on :5002 only (nginx answers 404 for /vortex/internal/) and re-hashes the bytes.
  - v7 (C-117 as built): the fetch takes the blob out of the store (first-fetch delete) and streams it in 256 KiB chunks with its Content-Length, without a copy. A taken blob stays counted against the 256 MB total until its buffer is freed: once the server has accepted the last chunk, or once the response is dropped on a client disconnect or a send error. An upload that would pass the total (stored + taken + booked bytes) is refused with 507.
- A bridge restart loses blobs in flight; the tool then returns UPLOAD_FAILED, which is retryable.

Uses
- analyze_screen capture.
- The analyze_camera webcam fallback.
- send_email attachments from Windows paths: a failed pull is an error, never a mail sent without the attachment.

Backup pull
- GET /vortex/desktop/backup/latest (PC-signed) streams the newest encrypted snapshot from jarvis_agent_snapshots (mounted read-only).
- v8 (C-122 as built, src/core/desktop/backup_pull.py), the node side:
  - destination %LOCALAPPDATA%\JARVIS\vps_backups (inside the K-76 sensitive set, so no laptop path tool can read it). Every snapshot is kept, nothing is deleted or overwritten; the same snapshot pulled twice is kept once, and a name clash with other content gets ' (n)'. A name the mirror would refuse becomes 'jarvis_snapshot_<UTC time>.bin';
  - download order: '.download.<random>.part' (created new), size check against Content-Length, Mark-of-the-Web, rename without overwriting. At most 64 GiB, and 1 GiB of the disk always stays free (else 'disk_full'). One pull at a time per folder (a '.pull.lock' file, taken over after 6 h); a second gets 'busy';
  - a file that looks like plaintext (SQLite, ZIP, gzip, tar or JSON) is kept but reported encrypted=false with a warning;
  - daily: an active-mode node task (never with --canary) pulls when the last successful pull is 24 h old or older, checked every hour, retried 1 h after a failure; on demand: 'agent_ctl backup pull' (K-53 v8). Both record run/desktop_backup_pull.json (last_success, last_size and the folder totals, or last_error). The daily task audits backup_pulled or backup_pull_failed (sizes and reason codes only). An on-demand pull writes no node audit row; its trace is agent_ctl's one backup_pull line in logs/agent_ctl.log (K-53 v8);
  - the on-demand pull loads the node config and the DPAPI-wrapped node key as the node does (the key never leaves the process) and signs with the clock offset the node last measured (run/desktop_node.json offset_s, when that status is at most a day old), else with the own clock.

#### K-74 · DESKTOP-STATUS (socketio-event+http-api) · owner: Claude
Event
- desktop_status = {online: bool, state: 'online'|'stale'|'offline'|'locked'|'panic', mode: 'off'|'read'|'full', locked: bool, voice_active: bool, node_id, version, git_sha, manifest_ok: bool, since, last_seen, rtt_ms_p50, busy_tool?, brain: 'vps'|'pc'}.
  - Presence stays on the node (K-76): there is no presence_s.
- The bridge builds it from the K-70 link alone, so it stays right with no agent peer connected:
  - node_id, version and git_sha come from the node's verified hello;
  - mode and locked come from the hello, then from each desktop_state notice, which also gives panic;
  - last_seen = the bridge's receive time of the last verified node message other than a ping or pong;
  - state, in this order:
    - offline while no node socket has a verified hello;
    - offline after a power notice suspend, shutdown or logoff, until a power resume notice, any later verified node message or the next hello;
    - else stale when last_seen is more than 25 s old;
    - else panic, locked or online;
  - online = state is online, locked or panic; since = when state last changed;
  - manifest_ok is false from a MANIFEST_MISMATCH alert notice until the next hello;
  - busy_tool = the tool of the oldest exec the bridge relayed to the node without its result;
  - rtt_ms_p50 = the median round trip, timed at the bridge, from an agent ping it relays to the node's pong;
  - voice_active and brain come from the bridge's own state.
  - v8 (as built): voice_active is true for 60 s after the last voice activity the bridge saw through /notify (a status START, a voice transcription, or user_speaking_sync true); its start is sent at once, its end within the 1 s status tick.
- The bridge sends it:
  - to K-70 agent peers as 'status';
  - v8 (C-122 as built): to the node as a 'status' hint right after its welcome and whenever voice_active, brain or active_job change (K-70 v8 Bridge hints), so the node's K-73 large-file rule never runs on a stale welcome snapshot;
  - to UI sockets on '/' as 'desktop_status' on every change, and in init_state.desktop_status;
  - inside GET /vortex/status as the 'desktop' block (session or agent credentials).
- Public GET /vortex/health stays {status, version, uptime_s} (K-43). It never carries presence, brain or vitals.

Notices (K-70: node → 'bridge', signed, not encrypted, never relayed)
- Each body is {kind, ...} with exactly that kind's fields.
  - Optional fields may be absent but never null. Anything else is refused: BAD_ARGS when building, check 8 at the bridge.
  - number: a JSON int or float, never a bool, range inclusive.
  - integer: an int, never a bool or float.
  - text: 1..N characters, all printable (Python str.isprintable(): no control, bidi, zero-width, private-use or unassigned characters, and no separator except the ASCII space).
- {kind:'vitals_pc', cpu, ram, disk, disk_label?, host?, cores?, ram_total_gb?}:
  - cpu, ram and disk are numbers 0..100;
  - disk_label is text ≤ 32; host is text ≤ 64; cores is an integer 1..4096; ram_total_gb is a number 0..65536;
  - sent every 10 s from the active-mode sensors (C-122).
  - v8 (C-122 as built): only while the link is connected. cpu, ram and disk are rounded to one decimal and clamped to 0..100; host is the node id (the K-70 id format: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-') and disk_label is 'Disk <letter>' (letters, digits, space, '.', '_', '-'), so neither can carry a path, a title or other free text. Battery, plugged and secs_left stay on the laptop.
- {kind:'desktop_state', mode: 'off'|'read'|'full', locked: bool, panic: bool}: sent after every hello, on every change, and every 10 s as the presence heartbeat. The heartbeat is a C-120 link duty in every node run mode.
- {kind:'power', state: 'suspend'|'resume'|'shutdown'|'logoff'}:
  - sent on the Windows notification;
  - after suspend the node sends nothing until it wakes. Then it sends a resume notice if the socket survived, or else a new hello;
  - shutdown and logoff are the last message on that connection.
- {kind:'alert', code, level, count?, message?, call_id?, tool?, peer?}:
  - count is an integer 1..1000000; message is text ≤ 200; peer is 'agent:<id>' or 'pc:<id>'; call_id and tool use the K-70 formats;
  - code and level are fixed pairs: SIGNATURE_INVALID and APPROVAL_INVALID are 'critical'; CLOCK_SKEW, MANIFEST_MISMATCH and DESKTOP_RATE_LIMITED are 'warning'. Any other pair is refused;
  - the node folds repeats of a code within 60 s into one notice, with count. v7 (C-120/C-121 as built): per code, the first alert notice goes out at once; the repeats within the next 60 s are sent as one notice with count (the fields of the latest repeat) when that window ends, and a further window opens only if repeats came. Notices that could not be sent while the link was down go out after the next hello.
- A notice is at most 4 KiB. It never carries arguments, results, paths, window titles, clipboard text, locations or presence. Those stay on the node, or go only to agent peers as encrypted events (K-70).
  - The library refuses any field outside the kind's list (BAD_ARGS, check 8), so there is no field for them.
  - It cannot see what a free-text field holds. Keeping that text out of alert message, host and disk_label is the node's duty, tested in C-121 and C-122.
- Storage:
  - the bridge keeps only the latest vitals_pc, desktop_state and power values, in the C-13 kv, overwritten in place;
  - it never writes notices or desktop_status history to its events or audit tables;
  - an alert notice becomes a system_alert and an audit row, and it is the only notice that writes an audit row.

Vitals
- The bridge emits each vitals_pc notice to UI sockets as vitals_pc {cpu, ram, disk, disk_label?, cores?, ram_total_gb?, host, ts}. host = node_id when the notice has none; ts = the bridge's receive time.
- The legacy vitals_update prefers a vitals_pc reading less than 30 s old; the bridge's own psutil figures are vitals_vps.
- The UI shows a stale state after 30 s.

Commands from the UI (tighten-only)
- ui_command 'desktop_stop' → node mode read, and every in-flight laptop call cancelled.
  - The bridge accepts it only from UI sockets (K-40 v4).
  - It persists it until a desktop_state notice or a hello reports mode read or off, and re-sends it after a node reconnect.
  - It sends the tighten-only control desktop_stop to the node and a stop_all hint to the agent peers, and emits desktop_status.
  - Only the laptop tray switches back to full (K-76).
- ui_command 'notification_ack' {id} → the K-77 delivery ledger.

Alerts (system_alert to the UI, an audit row, and a local toast on the laptop)
- system_alert = {id, severity: 'critical'|'warning'|'info', code, title, count, ts}.
  - title is the alert's message, or else a short text for the code.
  - Repeats of one code within 60 s are folded into one, with count.
  - v7 (C-116 as built): the bridge folds per (source, code), where source is 'bridge' for its own alerts and 'node' for the node's alert notices. The first alert of a key gets a new id, goes to the UI at once, writes its audit row and (bridge alerts only) goes to the node as an alert hint. A repeat within 60 s of that first alert adds its count to the same id: the growing count reaches the UI at most every 5 s, and the final count when the window closes. Every node alert notice writes its own audit row (capped); a bridge alert that repeated gets one more audit row with its total count when its window closes. A repeat after the 60 s window starts a new alert with a new id.
- critical: any signature or approval verification failure.
- warning: desktop_replaced, a new node_id, manifest drift, clock skew above 60 s, duplicate agent participants, rate-limit trips, more than 3 agent restarts per hour, memory above 4 GiB (warn) or 6 GiB (critical), disk below 30 GB (warn) or 15 GB (critical).
- info: laptop offline for more than 30 min while a UI is connected.
- Clock skew seen at the bridge: a node hello or notice whose signature verified, but which is refused only as stale or future, raises the clock-skew warning.
  - Its title states the measured skew: the message ts minus the bridge clock.
  - It never raises the critical alert, and it never counts as a failed verification for the per-IP limit (K-70 Rates).
  - Pings and pongs still pass the bridge, so the agent and the node measure the step themselves (K-70 check 5).
- Who raises them:
  - from cutover, the bridge (C-116): signature failures on '/desktop', desktop_replaced, a new node_id, rate-limit trips, and the clock skew above. Each one also goes to the node as an alert hint, which the node shows as a toast;
  - from cutover, the node (C-121): each alert is a local toast plus an alert notice, which the bridge turns into system_alert and an audit row;
  - C-134 adds the restart, memory, disk, duplicate-agent and offline alerts.

#### K-75 · AGENT-CONTAINERS (deploy) · owner: Claude
Image
- jarvis-agent:hostinger, built from deploy/hostinger/Dockerfile.agent:
  - FROM python:3.12-slim-trixie@sha256:<pinned digest>;
  - apt ffmpeg, nodejs, curl, ca-certificates, tzdata;
  - torch, torchaudio and torchvision +cpu from the PyTorch CPU index;
  - deploy/hostinger/requirements-agent.txt (the hybrid list without PyAudio, sounddevice, opencv-python/contrib, mediapipe, PyAutoGUI, pynput, pygetwindow, comtypes, pycaw, pywin32, pywhatkit, pygame, playsound; plus opencv-contrib-python-headless) with constraints-agent.txt;
  - ECAPA (fixed download script) and MiniLM baked in, readable by uid 10001 and loaded with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1;
  - media wrappers in /usr/local/jarvis-bin (nice/ionice only when JARVIS_MEDIA_PRIORITY=low);
  - USER 10001; WORKDIR /app.
- It is built on the VPS from the committed HEAD by the dedicated buildx builder 'jarvis-builder' (docker-container driver, --load).
- GIT_SHA is an image label and ENV only; it is never interpolated into compose 'environment:'.

Services (compose profile vps-brain)
- agent: container jarvis-agent, CMD python -m src.core.agent start --drain-timeout 20, health curl 127.0.0.1:8081/.
- agent-svc: container jarvis-agent-svc, CMD python -m src.core.agent_services, health 127.0.0.1:8083/health.
- Shared settings for both:
  - user 10001, init true, env_file .env.agent (root 600, never mounted), environment per K-72, networks jarvis-net, no published ports;
  - depends_on livekit started and ui-bridge healthy;
  - restart unless-stopped, stop_grace_period 60s (drain 20 s + job shutdown 20 s);
  - oom_score_adj 500, security_opt no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL, logging json-file 10m×3;
  - /tmp on the container disk (no tmpfs);
  - NO mem_limit, cpus or cpu_shares (user decision 2026-10-01); pids_limit only when the user approves it.

Volumes
- jarvis_agent_conversations:/app/conversations, jarvis_agent_chroma:/app/chroma_db, jarvis_agent_data:/app/data (identity dir 700, settings), jarvis_agent_backups:/app/backups, jarvis_agent_logs:/app/logs, jarvis_agent_snapshots:/app/snapshots (svc rw), jarvis_outputs:/app/Jarvis_Outputs, jarvis_shared:/app/Jarvis_Shared (agent rw, svc ro).
- The two existing shared volumes get a one-time chown to 10001 through 'docker compose -p jarvis run --rm --no-deps --user 0 --entrypoint chown agent'.

Bridge
- oom_score_adj 300; internal listener :5002 on jarvis-net only.
- Mounts jarvis_shared, jarvis_outputs and jarvis_agent_snapshots read-only; no agent log mount.
- env_file bridge.env after V2b.

URLs
- The agent uses LIVEKIT_URL ws://jarvis-livekit:7880 and UI_BRIDGE_URL http://jarvis-bridge:5002.
- Media hairpins to the advertised IP. If the canary probe fails: rtc.advertise_internal_ip true; last resort, host networking for the agent only.

Deploys
- Always name the services ('up -d --no-deps <svc>').
- The gate: healthy within 180 s, /worker agent_name, LiveKit 'worker registered', agent_hello on /desktop via :5002, net_guard self-test, offline model load, other-apps smoke diff identical.
- Downloads are refused below 20 GB free disk; deploys warn below 30 GB and fail below 15 GB.
v36 (C-126, as built): deploy/hostinger/Dockerfile.agent: python:3.12-slim-trixie pinned by its index digest; torch, torchaudio and torchvision --no-deps from the CPU index, then requirements-agent.txt with constraints-agent.txt, then pip check; pystray excluded; ECAPA and MiniLM (pinned revision, HF_HOME=/app/pretrained_models/huggingface) baked before the code and owned by uid 10001 in their own layer (SpeechBrain 1.0.1 rewrites its custom.py link at every load); the build runs IMPORT_OK and scripts/models/check_models.py --expect-uid 10001 offline as uid 10001; USER 10001; HEALTHCHECK 'env -i curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8081/' (agent-svc :8083/health); /usr/local/jarvis-bin/{ffmpeg,ffprobe,yt-dlp} is one sh wrapper that runs the real program from /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin or /bin, under nice -n 10 (and ionice idle) only with JARVIS_MEDIA_PRIORITY=low (D9, opt-in; a priority, never a limit); GIT_SHA (ARG, label, ENV) last. Compose: agent and agent-svc are in the profile vps-brain, so no bare 'up' starts them and every deploy names its services with up -d --no-deps --no-build --pull never; no build: section (jarvis-builder only); env_file {path: .env.agent, required: true}; init false, set explicitly (python is PID 1 and makes itself non-dumpable; docker-init would keep every .env.agent secret in a dumpable /proc/1/environ, and an unset value takes the daemon default); no CPU or RAM limits; healthcheck start_period 120 s (agent) and 60 s (agent-svc); agent-svc logs to logs/jarvis_agent_svc.log and handles SIGTERM itself (C-125). The compose file needs a non-empty JARVIS_BRAIN in the VPS .env (${JARVIS_BRAIN:?}): without it every compose command refuses, so it is set before the first deploy that ships this file; rollback.sh --env keeps the live JARVIS_BRAIN and COMPOSE_PROFILES lines when the restored hostinger.env predates them; deploy.sh --gate-only fails when compose config fails. The one-time chown: docker compose -p jarvis run --rm --no-deps --user 0 --cap-add CHOWN --entrypoint chown agent -R 10001:10001 /app/Jarvis_Outputs /app/Jarvis_Shared (and agent-svc for /app/snapshots). Build records go to /root/jarvis-backups/builds/<UTC>/.
v41 (C-127, as built):
- Bridge: env_file stays [.env, {path: bridge.env, required: false}] until C-18 drops .env. Since V2b, bridge.env carries the bridge's own names and settings (K-47 v41) and .env holds no agent secret. V2b changes only the env files and recreates ui-bridge alone from its image with its running GIT_SHA (up -d --no-deps --no-build --pull never --force-recreate ui-bridge), then the gate.
- backup_vps.sh also copies .env.agent to env.agent (mode 600). It is never inside opt-jarvis-agent.tgz, and the PC mirror streams every backup without it. It writes env_layout lines into MANIFEST.txt: each env file the containers read (.env, bridge.env, .env.agent), present or absent, with the names it assigns, never a value; a UTF-8 byte order mark is read past.
- rollback.sh's env layout check, before any change: it compares the target's recorded layout (for an older backup, the names of its env copies) with the live files its services read: ui-bridge reads .env and bridge.env, livekit reads .env, agent and agent-svc read .env and .env.agent, and .env counts whenever --code brings back another compose file. JARVIS_BRAIN and COMPOSE_PROFILES never count.
  - A different layout is refused (exit 1) unless --with-env.
  - An unknown layout (a --tag without its backup folder) is refused unless --layout-unknown-ok; --with-env is then refused (exit 64).
  - A backup folder and --tag are never combined (exit 64).
- rollback.sh --with-env (alias --env) puts back, from one backup:
  - the image tags;
  - docker-compose.yml, whenever .env goes back;
  - only the env files that the services of the rollback read: .env from hostinger.env, bridge.env, .env.agent from env.agent, plus root.env; mode 600.
  - A live bridge.env that the target never had is moved aside (bridge.env.pre-rollback-<UTC>). The live .env.agent stays when the backup has none.
  - The live JARVIS_BRAIN and COMPOSE_PROFILES lines are written back into a restored .env, and the live DESKTOP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY and DESKTOP_PC_PUBLIC_KEY (in .env.agent also DESKTOP_AGENT_SIGNING_KEY) into the restored files.
  - The shared values AGENT_TOKEN, BRIDGE_HMAC_SECRET, LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET, LIVEKIT_PC_API_KEY and LIVEKIT_PC_API_SECRET are compared by digest on the VPS before any change (the dry run too). A difference is refused (exit 1, names only) unless --shared-values-differ-ok, which the printed undo then carries too.
  - Every rollback runs backup_vps.sh pre-rollback first and prints its undo.
- The env tools keep their backups in /root/jarvis-backups/env/<UTC>-<label>/ (folder 700, files 600), never in a 2* folder beside backup_vps.sh's.
- V6, the announced LiveKit window: livekit's environment becomes LIVEKIT_KEYS: "${LIVEKIT_API_KEY}: ${LIVEKIT_API_SECRET}\n${LIVEKIT_PC_API_KEY:?run livekit_pc_pair.py create}: ${LIVEKIT_PC_API_SECRET:?run livekit_pc_pair.py create}" (two keys, one per line), deployed with --services livekit. Until then compose names one pair. The PC pair is revoked on its own (livekit_pc_pair.py revoke, then a livekit recreate); the bridge, the VPS agent and the browsers keep the main pair.

#### K-76 · DESKTOP-POLICY + APPROVALS + STOPS (policy) · owner: Claude
Authority
- The Desktop Node enforces the laptop-side rules: classes, the Windows-lock pause, paths, captures, origins, stops and caps.
- Approvals for risky laptop actions happen in the agent before the exec is sent: the C-28 ConfirmFlow (K-14), that is the dashboard Allow or, where this contract allows it, a spoken yes. User decision D3 (2026-10-02): the laptop shows no approval prompt and needs no manual step.
- The effective risk is the strictest of: the node class, K-16 (decorator metadata) and K-45. A confirm_level setting may only make it stricter.
- A call is confirm-class when its class is messaging, code_exec, availability or exposure, when its K-16 risk resolves to medium or high, or when K-45 lists it as HIGH. K-45 MEDIUM input tools keep running with a UI toast and an audit row.

Modes and session state
- Modes: off | read | full. The node starts in full as soon as it runs (logon autostart, D11), unless run/desktop_state.json holds a panic latch, a remote stop or a tray Off/Read choice: these survive a reboot or logon, the node then starts in that mode (off or read), and desktop_status shows it on the Laptop chip until the tray Full clears it.
- Remote callers (UI 'desktop_stop', chat, agent, bridge) can only tighten. Loosening (full after a remote stop or a panic, desktop_control back on) happens only at the laptop (tray, or the PC root .env for desktop_control), never from the UI or the bridge.
- Windows lock (WTS session notifications): while the session is locked, every call that needs the desktop_input lock (K-16) returns DESKTOP_LOCKED without running, because Windows blocks input injection then, and captures are refused; other calls run under their normal rules. Unlock resumes input automatically, with no user action. Sleep or logoff takes the node offline (DESKTOP_OFFLINE) until resume or logon. The node first sends a K-70 power notice (suspend, shutdown or logoff), so desktop_status shows offline at once (K-74). After a suspend it sends nothing until it wakes; shutdown and logoff are the last message of the connection.
- Kill switch: JARVIS_DESKTOP_CONTROL=false (config.desktop_control_enabled, K-15) refuses every actuation with DESKTOP_CONTROL_DISABLED; de-escalation still runs. The node reads it from the PC root .env at start and within seconds of a change (K-72 settings source); the UI can only turn it off, and only after C-59.
- Check order on the node: kill switch, panic, mode and Windows lock first, then class and approval, then origin, then paths. A canary or probe call therefore gets a state or approval refusal first, and nothing actuates. Every refusal before the start, with its K-76 code, reaches the agent as the K-70 refusal ack {accepted:false, code}, never as a result (v5). A call that started ends with its result.
- Presence = genuine local input (keyboard/mouse hook events without LLKHF_INJECTED/LLMHF_INJECTED) within JARVIS_PRESENCE_WINDOW_S; captures use JARVIS_CAPTURE_PRESENCE_S. Presence stays on the node (v5). No presence value goes to the bridge or the agents: the hello, the notices and desktop_status carry none.
- Hook threads (v7, C-121 as built, presence.py): the low-level hook callbacks (WH_KEYBOARD_LL, WH_MOUSE_LL) and the WTS lock window only record (the presence time; the lock flag at once, so the lock state is right immediately) and enqueue the event. The key and lock listeners (the panic hotkey with its run/desktop_state.json write and cancel-all, the lock pause) run on a separate dispatcher thread, in arrival order, because Windows removes a low-level hook without notice when its callback takes longer than LowLevelHooksTimeout. A lock or unlock also resets the panic combo, since the secure desktop swallows the key-ups.

Run time (v7, C-121 as built: policy.guard_input_runs, keygate.py, executor.py)
- Every K-16 desktop_input tool (executor.K16_DESKTOP_INPUT: open_app, save_notepad, create_template_code, write_custom_code, edit_notepad_file_tool, append_notepad_file_tool, move_cursor_tool, mouse_click_tool, scroll_cursor_tool, press_key_tool, swipe_gesture_tool, press_hotkey_tool, type_text_tool, type_code_animation_tool, automate_whatsapp) takes the node's desktop_input lock, whatever its decorator says, and holds it for its whole run, until the call's thread work has ended, so two input calls never overlap. A lock not free within the exec's lock_wait_s gives DESKTOP_BUSY; thread work of a cancelled call still running 10 s after the cancel makes the executor degraded, and every input-lock call gets DESKTOP_DEGRADED until that work ends.
- Right before the run, with the lock held, the foreground rules are judged again (recheck_foreground): the state codes (kill switch, panic, off/read, Windows lock); PROTECTED_WINDOW when a shell, terminal, IDE or JARVIS window is in front and the call sends its keys to the window in front (the self-focus tools below are exempt here); APPROVAL_REQUIRED when the keystrokes would now reach a launch surface or messaging app the call's approval does not cover. A state code decides at once; PROTECTED_WINDOW or APPROVAL_REQUIRED gets up to 3 looks 0.2 s apart (a window that was just opened or closed may still take the focus) and the last one decides. A refusal here releases the lock and ends the call with result status 'not_started', effect 'none' and that code (its ack {accepted:true} had already gone; WAL state never_started), one 'desktop_recheck_refused' audit line, no toast and no alert. A re-check that raises fails closed (DESKTOP_REJECTED).
- A call that passes is pinned to the foreground judged for it: its window handle and protection class (protected, code_exec, messaging or input), so a title that changes while typing is no change, but another window or a tab that turns into a messaging app is.
- Chunks: type_text_tool when it types key by key (force_typing, or a text of at most 50 characters that is all ASCII; otherwise it pastes with one Ctrl+V, which is sent whole) and type_code_animation_tool (at most 6000 characters; its part after the first 1500 characters is one paste through type_text_tool when that part is longer than 50 characters or not ASCII, else it is typed in chunks too) are sent in chunks of at most 16 characters (INPUT_CHUNK_CHARS) that type exactly what the one call would have typed. Every other input-lock call (a key, a hotkey, a click, a move, a scroll, the self-focus tools) is one chunk. Before each chunk verify_input_run checks the state codes and the foreground rules again, and the pinned identity: another handle or protection class gives APPROVAL_REQUIRED.
- Foreground watchdog: while a chunk of type_text_tool or type_code_animation_tool runs, the foreground is looked at every 50 ms (watch_input_run): the state codes, PROTECTED_WINDOW, and APPROVAL_REQUIRED for a launch surface or messaging app the approval does not cover. The window the call started from is exempt until the focus first leaves it, and an unreadable foreground (a window switch) refuses only after 3 looks in a row. On a refusal the call's keys are blocked at once (keystroke gate) and the chunk's task is cancelled. Single key, hotkey, click, move, scroll and swipe calls get no watchdog.
- Self-focus tools (policy.SELF_FOCUS_TOOLS: open_app, save_notepad, create_template_code, write_custom_code, edit_notepad_file_tool, append_notepad_file_tool, automate_whatsapp; open_app only when its command asks it to write something) move the focus to their own window before they type, so they are judged per key at key time instead (judge_input_key). The keystroke gate sits in front of PyAutoGUI (its failSafeCheck, which PyAutoGUI calls before every key and mouse action) and pynput (Controller.press, used by type_text_tool and the clipboard's Ctrl+V); the node imports both before such a call so a lazily imported library is gated from its first key. Each key is judged against the window that has the focus at that moment: the state codes; PROTECTED_WINDOW (also the window they started from, when the focus never moved); APPROVAL_REQUIRED for a launch surface or messaging app the approval does not cover, and for a browser while their text holds a javascript: URL. A protected window in front at their start does not refuse them, and where the focus goes after their last key refuses nothing. The watchdog's looks are their fallback only when no gated input library could be loaded.
- A refused key never reaches the OS: the gate raises InputBlocked instead of it, a refused pynput press first releases the keys that controller still holds down (a refused Ctrl+V never leaves Ctrl pressed; releases are never refused), and every later key of that call is refused too. Keys of other calls and keys outside any call are never blocked or judged.
- On a refusal while running, nothing more is sent and the call ends with result status 'failed', effect 'possible' once a chunk had been sent (else 'none'), and the run-time code: DESKTOP_LOCKED, DESKTOP_PANIC, DESKTOP_CONTROL_DISABLED, DESKTOP_READ_ONLY, PROTECTED_WINDOW, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, or DESKTOP_REJECTED when a verify, watch or key judge itself fails (fails closed). This holds also when the tool swallowed the cancel or caught the refused key. The policy writes one 'desktop_input_interrupted' audit line (call_id, tool and code; no arguments, no title) and shows no toast and raises no alert. A chunk that returns an error result ends the run with that result; a self-focusing call that sent all its keys ends 'completed' wherever the focus went after.
- De-escalation calls skip every run-time check.

Classes
- read: vitals, active window, Notepad list, page read, documents, pc.ping. Needs mode read or full.
- capture: pc.capture_screen, pc.capture_webcam. Needs presence or a session opt-in, plus a toast (D15); refused while the foreground title shows a sensitive path or a password manager.
- input: keys, mouse, typing, mapped open_app, Notepad typing, window min/max, play_*, automate_youtube, PinchTab actions. Needs mode full and adds no approval of its own (K-45 MEDIUM tools run with a toast). Calls that need the desktop_input lock pause while Windows is locked. Refused on protected windows (title prefixes 'JARVIS & ANNA', 'JARVIS-Agent-Worker', 'JARVIS-AGENT'; shells, terminals, IDEs).
- messaging: automate_whatsapp, typing into messaging apps. Needs mode full + the ConfirmFlow approval; the WHATSAPP_TEST_NUMBERS guard applies in live tests.
- code_exec: needs mode full + the ConfirmFlow approval as HIGH (dashboard Allow only). It covers:
  - run_cmd_command (always high per K-45);
  - write_custom_code with auto_run;
  - open_app with an unmapped or executable target;
  - Win+*, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Alt+F11, F12, Ctrl+Shift+I/J;
  - typing into the Run dialog, Explorer address bar, Start/Search, taskmgr, regedit, mmc, consoles, Office VBA or DevTools;
  - opening executables, scripts, shortcuts or archives.
- availability: shutdown, restart, sleep, recycle bin, force close, close with more than one match. Needs mode full + the ConfirmFlow approval.
- exposure: file server, pc.read_file. Needs mode full + the ConfirmFlow approval, whose summary names the path.
- de-escalation: cancel_shutdown, stop_file_access_server, chrome_browser_close. Always allowed, even during panic.

Path policy (mandatory argument hooks)
- edit/append_notepad_file: a basename only, inside Jarvis_Outputs.
- open_notepad_file, folder_file, play_file, Windows zip_files and pc.read_file: resolve_in_roots(open_roots) plus is_sensitive_path, extended with the repo except Jarvis_Outputs, .venv*, any *.pth, the Startup folders, %LOCALAPPDATA%\JARVIS, ~/.ssh, *.env, id_*, .coord, chroma_db, conversations, logs and password-manager data. This keeps the node's own keys, pinned code and policy state out of reach.
- pc.read_file is limited to 25 MB.

Approvals (ConfirmFlow in the agent; no prompt on the laptop)
- ui: the dashboard Allow (K-14 confirm_response), for any class.
- voice: a spoken yes accepted by the broker on a final voice transcript (C-75), medium risk only, never code_exec, and for laptop actions only on a voice-ID-verified turn (D20), so it is refused until enrollment.
- The agent sends a confirm-class exec only after the approval and puts approval {confirm_id, channel, risk, args_sha256} inside the signed, encrypted body. The node runs it only when args_sha256 matches the exec; a missing approval gives APPROVAL_REQUIRED and a mismatch gives APPROVAL_INVALID, and nothing runs.
- v7 (C-121 as built, policy._approval_verdict), in this order:
  - no approval object → APPROVAL_REQUIRED;
  - APPROVAL_INVALID (the critical K-74 alert notice, raised once per refused exec by the node, plus a local toast) only when the approval does not verify: its args_sha256 differs from the exec's, or it is malformed: confirm_id missing or blank, risk missing or not one of low/medium/high, channel not 'ui' or 'voice' (the bridge never approves), or a voice approval whose risk is not medium or that lacks voice_id_verified: true (the agent sets it inside the signed body for a voice-ID-verified turn, D20);
  - a valid approval (matching args_sha256, a confirm_id, a known risk and channel) whose risk is below the call's effective risk now, for example a medium approval for a call the node raised to code_exec (high), or a spoken yes for code_exec or for an effective risk other than medium → APPROVAL_REQUIRED, never APPROVAL_INVALID: the agent asks again through ConfirmFlow at the higher risk and re-sends the exec with the new approval;
  - a bad signature never reaches this check: K-70 check 4 drops the message (DL_REJECT, the critical SIGNATURE_INVALID alert), and no ack is sent for it.
- Dynamic risk found on the node (a launch surface, an unmapped open_app target, a command outside the read-only allow-list) also returns APPROVAL_REQUIRED; the agent turns it into a ConfirmFlow item and re-sends the exec with the approval. Nothing is held or prompted on the laptop.
- The ConfirmFlow summary for a laptop action shows the normalised arguments (control, bidi and zero-width characters escaped; whitespace collapsed; metacharacters highlighted).
- The bridge never signs approvals or loosening controls, and it cannot forge an approval reference because it cannot sign as the agent. A dashboard Allow reaches the agent through the bridge's ConfirmFlow routing (C-29, live before cutover), so a compromised bridge could forge one for a pending item; laptop-verified owner approvals (C-133, X-68) would close that gap and are optional and deferred by D3.

Origins
- Actuation = a call in the input, messaging, code_exec, availability or exposure class.
